imitamen.definition: imitāmen inis, n imitor, an imitation, likeness, image: Somnia, quae veras aequent imitamine formas, O.—Plur., O.

imitamentum.definition: (imitāmentum ī), n imitor, an imitation, copy.—Only plur: veterum Romanorum, Ta.: tristitiae, Ta.

imitatio.definition: imitātiō ōnis, f imitor, a copying, imitation: virtutis: virtus imitatione digna: nihil ostentationis imitationis adferre, affectation.

imitator.definition: imitātor ōris, m imitor, an imitator, copyist, mimic: imitatores faceti: nec desilies imitator in artum, H.: laborum meorum: stulti sapiens, O.

imitatrix.definition: imitātrīx īcis, f imitator, she that imitates: boni (voluptas): gloriae.

imitatus.definition: imitātus adj. P. of imitor, fictitious: sim<*> lacra: voluptas, O.

imitor.definition: imitor ātus, āre, freq. 2 IC-, to imitate, act like, copy after, seek to resemble, counterfeit, mimic: genus ad omnia imitanda aptissimum, Cs.: in gloriā Paulum: aliquem imitando effingere: imitari quam invidere bonis…

immadesco.definition: (immadēscō or in-m-) duī, —, ere, inch, to become wet.—Only perf: sanguine terram, O.

immane.definition: immāne (inm-) adv. immanis, frightfully, fiercely, savagely: leo hians, V.: sonat fluctus, V.

immanis.definition: immānis (inm-) e, adj. with comp. and sup. 1 MA-, monstrous, enormous, immense, huge, vast: corporum magnitudo, Cs.: praeda: pocula: tegumen leonis, V.: studium loquendi, excessive, O.: avaritia, S.: impulsae praeceps…

immanitas.definition: immānitās (inm-) ātis, f immanis, monstrous size, hugeness, vastness, excess: vitiorum.— Monstrousness, enormity, heinousness, savageness, fierceness, cruelty, barbarism: immanitate bestias vincere: gentes immanitate …

immansuetus.definition: immānsuētus (in-m-) adj. with sup, untamed, wild, savage: Cyclops, O.: (ventus) immansuetissime, O.

immaturitas.definition: immātūritās (inm-) ātis, f immaturus, untimely haste: tanta.

immaturus.definition: immātūrus (in-m-) adj., untimely, unripe, immature, premature: mors: tibi inmaturo vita erepta est, S.: filius obiit, H.: amor, unseasonable, L.

immedicabilis.definition: immedicābilis (in-m-) e, adj., incurable: volnus, O.: telum, i. e. fatal, V.

immemor.definition: immemor (in-m-) oris, abl. orī, adj., unmindful, not thinking, forgetful, regardless, negligent, heedless: ingenium: mens, Ct.: Instamus tamen inmemores, V.: rerum a me gestarum: benefici, T.: coniugis, H.: in testand…

immemoratus.definition: immemorātus (in-m-) adj., unmentioned, untold: iuvat immemorata ferentem legi, i. e. novelties, H.

immensitas.definition: immēnsitās (inm-) ātis, f immensus, immeasurableness, immensity: latitudinum.—Plur: camporum.

immensum1.definition: immēnsum (inm-) ī, n immensus, a boundless extent, vastness, immensity: per immensum actus, O.: mons in immensum editus, S.: ad immensum multitudinis speciem augere, L.

immensum2.definition: immēnsum (inm-) adv. immensus, without end, exceedingly, immensely: creverat, O.

immensus.definition: immēnsus (in-m-) adj., immeasurable, boundless, endless, vast, immense: magnitudo regionum: domus, O.: fines ingeni: argenti pondus et auri, H.: agmen aquarum, V.: tempore immenso.— Fig., vast, measureless, boundless,…

immerens.definition: immerēns (in-m-) entis, adj., undeserving, innocent: dominus, H.: offerre iniuriam tibi inmerenti, T.

immergo.definition: immergō (in-m-) sī, sus, ere, to dip, plunge, sink, immerse, submerge: immersus in flumen: virum spumosā undā, V.—Fig.: se in Asuvi consuetudinem, to insinuate.

immerito.definition: immeritō (inm-) adv. with sup. immeritus, undeservedly, unjustly, without cause: accusare me inmeritissumo, T.: si immerito, si misera, etc.

immeritus.definition: immeritus (in-m-) adj., undeserving, guiltless, innocent, without fault: Delicta maiorum immeritus lues, H.: gens, V.: paries, H.: inmeriti ultor parentis, O.: immeriti mori, who deserve not to die, H.—Undeserved, unm…

immersabilis.definition: immersābilis (inm-) e, adj. 2 in+merso, not to be sunk, unconquerable: adversis undis, H.

immetatus.definition: immētātus (in-m-) adj. measureless, vast: iugera, H.

immigro.definition: immigrō (in-m-) āvī, ātus, āre, to remove, migrate, change abode: in domum.—Fig., of words: immigrasse in suum (locum) diceres, i. e. have found their appropriate use.

immineo.definition: immineō (in-m-) —, —, ēre, to project over, lean towards, hang down over, overhang, overarch: Quos super silex Imminet, V.: imminente lunā , shining overhead, H.: in ore impuri hominis imminens, bending towards: gestu…

imminuo.definition: imminuō (in-m-) uī, ūtus, ere, to lessen, diminish: copias.— To weaken, impair, enfeeble: mente inminutā, S.—Fig., to lessen, diminish, abate: tempus mora inminuerat, S.: imminuitur aliquid de voluptate: se dolor immi…

imminutio.definition: imminūtiō (inm-) ōnis, f imminuo, a lessening, weakening, impairing, injuring: corporis, i. e. mutilation.—Fig.: dignitatis.— Esp., as a figure of speech, understatement, extenuation.

imminutus.definition: imminūtus (inm-) adj. P. of imminuo, weak: mens, narrow, Ta.

immisceo.definition: immisceō (in-m-) miscuī, mīxtus, ēre, to mix in, intermix, intermingle, blend: nives caelo prope inmixtae, L.: summis ima, O.: se nubi atrae, V. —Of boxers: manūs manibus, entwine, V.—Pass, to be mingled, be associate…

immiserabilis.definition: immiserābilis (in-m-) e, adj., unpitied: captiva pubes, H.

immisericorditer.definition: 'immisericorditer adv. immisericors, unmercifully: factum a vobis, T.'

immissio.definition: immissiō (inm-) ōnis, f inmitto, a letting grow, letting alone: sarmentorum.

immitis.definition: immītis (in-m-) e, adj. with comp, not mellow, harsh, unripe, sour: uva, H.—Rough, rude, harsh, hard, severe, stern, fierce, savage, inexorable: naturā et moribus, L.: tyrannus (i. e. Pluto), V.: Glycera, H.: oculi, O…

immitto.definition: immittō (in-m-) īsī, īssus, ere, to send in, let in, throw into, admit, introduce: immissus in urbem: servos ad spoliandum fanum: corpus in undas, O.: in terram (navem), stranded, L.: canalibus aqua inmissa, Cs.: fera…

immo.definition: immō (not īmō), adv. for * ipsimō; ipse. I. In contradiction or denial, no indeed, by no means, on the contrary, nay, in reality: An. ubi? domin? Ch. immo apud libertum, T.: dictum puta, Nempe . . . Si. immo aliud, na…

immobilis.definition: immōbilis (in-m-) e, adj. with comp, immovable: terra: His immobilior scopulis, heard-hearted , O.—Fig., unmoved: ardet Ausonia immobilis ante, V.

immoderate.definition: immoderātē (inm-) adv. with comp. immoderatus, without measure, by no rule: vox profusa.—Fig., immoderately, extravagantly: vivere: abuti nostrā facilitate: ferre immoderatius casum.

immoderatio.definition: immoderātiō (inm-) ōnis, f immoderatus, want of moderation, excess: verborum.

immoderatus.definition: immoderātus (in-m-) adj., boundless, immeasurable: aether.— Fig., unrestrained, unbridled, excessive, immoderate: homo: ne inmoderatus abundes, unduly officious, H.: fortitudo, S.: potus et pastus: tempestates.—Plur n…

immodeste.definition: immodestē adv. immodestus, immoderately, shamelessly: gloriari, L.

immodestia.definition: 'immodestia (inm-) ae, f immodestus, intemperate conduct, insubordination: publicanorum, extortion, Ta.: militum, N.'

immodestus.definition: 'immodestus (in-m-) adj., unrestrained, excessive, shameless: in vino, T.: genus iocandi.'

immodice.definition: immodicē adv. immodicus, beyond measure, excessively: gloriari, L.: potestate uti, L.

immodicus.definition: immodicus (in-m-) adj., beyond bounds, enormous, huge: rostrum, O.: tuber, O.—Fig., excessive, unrestrained, extravagant, immoderate: in numero augendo, given to exaggeration, L.: linguā, L.: laetitiae, Ta.: animi, Ta…

immodulatus.definition: immodulātus (in-m-) adj., unrhythmical, inharmonious: poëmata, H.

immolatio.definition: immolātiō (inm-) ōnis, f immolo, a sacrificing, sacrifice: immolationis tempus: immolationes nefandae, Ta.

immolator.definition: immolātor (in-m-) ōris, m immolo, a sacrificer: immolatoris fortuna.

immolitus.definition: immōlītus (in-m-) P., built up, erected.— Plur. n. as subst: in loca publica inaedificata immolitave habere, buildings or structures, L.

immolo.definition: immolō (in-m-) āvī, ātus, āre, to sprinkle with sacrificial meal; hence, to make a sacrifice, offer, sacrifice, immolate: cum Sulla immolaret: Musis bovem: animalia capta, Cs.: homines, Cs.: cum pluribus dis immolatur…

immordeo.definition: (immordeō or in-m-) —, sus, ēre, to bite into.—Only P. pass.: immorso collo, Pr.: stomachus pernā immorsus, i. e. stimulated, H.

immorior.definition: immorior (in-m-) mortuus, ī, to die in, die upon, fall upon in death: sorori, O.: ipsis aquis, O.: immoritur studiis, pines away over, H.

immortalis.definition: immortālis (in-m-) e, adj., undying, immortal: corpus: di, the gods, Cs., C.: pro deūm immortalium! T.—Imperishable, eternal, endless: (imperatorum) memoria: laudes, Ta.: fructus vestri in me amoris: opera, L.: nemo i…

immortalitas.definition: immortālitās (inm-) ātis, f immortalis, exemption from death, immortality, endless life: animorum: vita immortalitate cedens caelestibus. —Plur: hominum, immortal natures.—Imperishableness, imperishable fame, undying …

immotus.definition: immōtus (in-m-) adj., unmoved, immovable, motionless: (arbor) immota manet, V.: Ceres, O.: mare, Ta.: voltus, Ta.—Fig., unmoved, unshaken, undisturbed, steadfast, firm: manent inmota tuorum Fata tibi, V.: animus, Ta.:…

immugio.definition: immūgiō (in-m-) iī, —, īre, to bellow in, resound inwardly: immugiit Aetna cavernis, V.: regia luctu, V.

immulgeo.definition: (immulgeō or in-m-) —, —, ēre, to milk into.— Only P. praes.: ubera labris, V.

immundus.definition: immundus (in-m-) adj. with comp, unclean, impure, dirty, fllthy, foul: ancillula inluvie, T.: canis, H.: nilo inmundior, Ct.: fraudatis lucernis, i. e. with lamp-oil, H.—Plur f. as subst, unclean women, C.—Of language…

immunio.definition: immūniō (inm-) īvī, —, īre, to fortify: praesidium, Ta.

immunis.definition: immūnis (inm-) e, adj. 2 MV-, not bound, free from obligation, disengaged, unemployed: non est inhumana virtus neque inmunis, unsocial: sedens ad pabula, idle, V.: tellus, untilled, O.: operum famulae, O.—Making no re…

immunitas.definition: immūnitās (inm-) ātis (gen plur. tātium, C.), f immunis, exemption from burdens, immunity, privilege: omnium rerum, Cs.: provinciae.— Fig.: magni muneris.

immunitus.definition: immūnītus (in-m-) adj., unfortified, undefended: oppida, L.: via, unpaved.

immurmuro.definition: immurmurō (in-m-) —, —, āre, to murmur at, murmur against: silvis immurmurat Auster, V.: totum immurmurat agmen, mutter reproachfully, O.

immutabilis.definition: immūtābilis (in-m-) e, adj. with comp, unchangeable, unalterable, immutable: causae: spatia: ratio, L.: concordi populo nihil immutabilius.

immutabilitas.definition: immūtābilitās (inm-) ātis, f immutabilis, unchangeableness, immutability.

immutatio.definition: immūtātiō (inm-) ōnis, f immuto, an interchange, substitution: verborum: ordinis.—In rhet., a metonymy, transferred meaning.

immuto.definition: immūtō (in-m-) āvī, ātus, āre, to change, alter, transform: inmutarier Ex amore, T.: me inmutatum videt, my mood, T.: inmutata urbis facies erat, S.: isti color immutatus est: me tibi: meam figuram, O.: aliquid de ins…

impacatus.definition: impācātus (inp-) adj. 2 in+pacatus, not peaceable, warlike: Iberi, V.

impar.definition: impār (in-p-) aris (abl. imparī; twice impare, V.), adj., uneven, unequal, dissimilar: numerus, odd: numero deus impare gaudet, V.: Musae, H.: ludere par impar, odd or even, H.: mensae erat pes tertius impar, O.: toga…

imparatus.definition: imparātus (in-p-) adj. with sup, not ready, unprepared, unprovided, unfurnished: Ut ne inparatus sim, T.: res p., S.: adgredi ad dicendum: inermem atque imparatum adoriuntur, off his guard: breve tempus longum est imp…

impariter.definition: 'impariter adv. impar, unequally: Versibus iunctis, i. e. in hexameters and pentameters, H.'

impastus.definition: impāstus (in-p-) adj., unfed, hungry: leo, V.

impatiens.definition: impatiēns (in-p-) entis, adj., that cannot bear, intolerant, impatient, submissive: viae, O.: volneris, V.: impatiens expersque viri, avoiding, O.: irae, ungovernable, O.: corpus laborum, O.: (terra) arborum, Ta.

impatienter.definition: 'impatienter (in-p-) adv. with comp, with impatience: indoluit, Ta.: captivitatem impatientius timere, Ta.'

impatientia.definition: 'impatientia (inp-) ae, f impatiens, impatience, incapacity: silentii, Ta.: ad impatientiam delabi, i. e. weakness, Ta.'

impavide.definition: impavidē adv. impavidus, fearlessly, intrepidly: exhausto poculo, L.

impavidus.definition: 'impavidus (in-p-) adj., fearless, undaunted, intrepid, unterrified: pueri, V.: Impavidum (illum) ferient ruinae, H.: pectora, L.: gens ingenio, L.'

impedimentum.definition: impedīmentum (inp-) ī, n impedio, a hinderance, impediment: impedimenta naturae diligentiā superare: esse impedimenti loco, Cs.: mi inpedimento estis, T.: libertati tempora sunt impedimento.—Plur, travelling equipage,…

impedio.definition: impediō (inp-) īvī, ītus, īre PED-, to entangle, ensnare, shackle, hamper, hinder, hold fast: Impediunt vincula nulla pedes, O.: illis Crura, O. —To clasp, bind, encircle, embrace. narrare parantem Impedit amplexu, O.…

impeditio.definition: impedītiō (inp-) ōnis, f impedio, a hinderance, obstruction: curarum.

impeditus.definition: impedītus (inp-) adj. with comp. and sup. P. of impedio, hindered, embarrassed, obstructed, encumbered, burdened, impeded: impeditis hostibus propter onera, Cs.: comitatus: agmen, L.: magnam partem eorum impeditam int…

impello.definition: impellō (in-p-) pulī, pulsus, ere. I. To strike against, push, drive, smite, strike, reach: montem Impulit in latus, V.: inpulsas tentavit pollice chordas, O.: manu portas, V.: Impellunt animae lintea, swell, H.: aura…

impendeo.definition: impendeō (in-p-) —, —, ēre, to hang over, overhang: ut (gladius) impenderet illius cervicibus: saxum Tantalo: iter difficile; mons altissimus inpendebat, commanded (it), Cs.—Fig., to be at hand, be near, be imminent, …

impendio.definition: impendiō (inp-) adv. abl. of impendium, by a great deal, very much: magis, far more, T., C.

impendium.definition: impendium (inp-) ī, n impendo, money laid out, outlay, cost, charge, expense: quaestum sibi instituere sine impendio: tantulo impendio victoria stetit, Cu.—Money paid for a loan, interest, usury: plebes impendiis debi…

impendo.definition: impendō (in-p-) pendī, pēnsus, ere, to weigh out, lay out, expend: operam in eas res: certus sumptus impenditur: de vestro, L.: aegram gallinam amico, lay out the value of, Iu.—To expend, devote, employ, apply, use: a…

impenetrabilis.definition: impenetrābilis (in-p-) e, adj., not to be pierced, impenetrable: silex ferro, L.: tegimen adversus ictūs, Ta.—Unconquerable: pudicitia, Ta.

impensa.definition: impēnsa (inp-) ae, f impensus; sc. pecunia, disbursement, expenditure, outlay, cost, charge, expense: impensam fecimus in macrocolā: nullā impensā, without cost: nostra, O.: pecuniae, L.: parcere impensae, economize, …

impense.definition: impēnsē (inp-) adv. with comp. impensus, exceedingly, greatly, very much, earnestly, eagerly, zealously: invidere, T.: eo facio id impensius, quod, etc.: agere gratias, L.: consulere, V.: venerari numina, O.: accendi …

impensus.definition: impēnsus (inp-) adj. with comp. P. of impendo, ample, considerate, great: impenso pretio, dear, Cs., L.—As subst n. (sc. pretio): Lusciniae impenso coemptae, H.—Great, strong, vehement: voluntas bonorum: erga eos volu…

imperans.definition: imperāns (inp-) ntis, m P. of impero, a master, conqueror, ruler.

imperator.definition: imperātor (inp-) ōris, m impero, a commander-in-chief, general: imperatoris virtus, T.: invictus: partes imperatoris, Cs.: id est dominum, non inperatorem esse, S.—Imperator (a title conferred on a victorious general)…

imperatorius.definition: imperātōrius (inp-) adj. imperator, of a general: labor: partes, Cs.: consilium: ardor oculorum, commanding.—Of the chief of the empire, imperial: virtus, Ta.

imperatrix.definition: imperātrīx (inp-) īcis, f imperator, she who commands, a mistress.

imperatum.definition: imperātum ī, n P. of impero, a command, order: imperatum facit, obeys, Cs.: imperata facere, Cs.: ad imperatum non venire, according to orders, Cs.

impercussus.definition: 'impercussus (in-p-) adj., not struck: pedes, i. e. noiseless, O.'

imperditus.definition: 'imperditus (in-p-) adj., not destroyed, not slain: corpora, V.'

imperfectus.definition: imperfectus (in-p-) adj., unfinished, incomplete, imperfect, immature: reliquum corpus imperfectum reliquerunt: inperfectā re redire, having failed, Cs.: infans adhuc, O.: pars manebat, V.: cibus, i. e. undigested, Iu.

imperfossus.definition: 'imperfossus (inp-) adj. 2 in+perfossus, unpierced: ab omni ictu, O.'

imperiosus.definition: imperiōsus (inp-) adj. with comp. and sup. imperium, possessed of command, far-ruling, mighty, powerful, puissant: urbes: dictatura, L.: virga, i. e. the fasces, O.: sibi qui imperiosus, lord of himself, H.—Arbitrary,…

imperite.definition: imperītē adv. with comp. and sup. imperitus, unskilfully, ignorantly, awkwardly: facit: quid potuit dici imperitius?: imperitissime dictum.

imperitia.definition: imperītia (inp-) ae, f imperitus, inexperience, ignorance, awkwardness: legati, S.: pugnam imperitiā poscere, Ta.

imperito.definition: imperitō (inp-) āvī, ātus, āre, freq. impero, to command, govern, rule, be supreme: decem imperitabant, L.: plerāque Africā , S.: magnis legionibus, H.: nemori, V.: alteri populo cum bonā pace, L.: aequam Rem imperito…

imperitus.definition: imperītus (in-p-) adj. with comp. and sup, inexperienced, unversed, unfamiliar, not knowing, unacquainted with, unskilled, ignorant: homo, T.: callidum imperitus fraudasse dicitur: ne quis imperitior existimet, me, et…

imperium.definition: imperium (inp-) ī, n impero, a command, order, direction, injunction: meum Inperium exequi, T.: imperio parere, Cs.: Iovis, V.: imperiis deūm expositis, L.: Naturae imperio gemimus, cum, etc., Iu.—Command, authority, …

imperiuratus.definition: imperiūrātus (in-p-) adj., by which no false oath is taken: aquae (of the Styx), O.

impero.definition: imperō (inp-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 in+paro, to command, order, enjoin, bid, give an order: Pa. Iubesne? Ch. Iubeam? cogo atque impero, T.: sicuti inperabatur, consistunt, S.: velut deo imperante, Ta.: adeo ad imperandum, …

impertio.definition: impertiō (inp-) īvī, ītus, īre in+partio, to share with, give a part, communicate, bestow, impart: si quid novisti rectius istis, Candidus imperti, H.: oneris mei partem nemini: aliquid tibi sui consili: tibi multam s…

impertior.definition: impertior —, —, īrī, dep. collat. form of impertio, to take as a partner, make a sharer in: eram hoc malo, T.

impertita.definition: impertīta ōrum, n P. of impertio, favors, concessions: pro his impertitis, L.

imperturbatus.definition: imperturbātus (in-p-) adj., undisturbed, unruffled, calm: ō s, O.

impervius.definition: 'impervius (in-p-) adj., not to be traversed, impassable: amnis, O.: lapis ignibus, fire-proof, Ta.'

impes.definition: '(impes or inpes, petis) m in+PET-, violence, vehemence, force (only abl sing.): impete vasto ferri, O.: certo impete, O.'

impetibilis.definition: 'impetibilis (inp-, impatib-) e, adj. in+ patibilis, insufferable, intolerable: dolor.'

impetrabilis.definition: impetrābilis (inp-) e, adj. with comp. impetro, to be obtained, attainable, practicable: venia, L.: Iunoni votum facere impetrabile, Pr.: quo impetrabilior pax esset, L.

impetratio.definition: impetrātiō (inp-) ōnis, f impetro, an obtaining by request; hence, an entreaty: nostrae.

impetrio.definition: impetriō —, —, īre, desid. impetro, to seek through omens, inquire for by auspices: avibus res impetriri solebant: qui impetrire velit.

impetro.definition: impetrō (inp-) āvī, ātus, āre in+patro, to gain one's end, achieve, bring to pass, effect, get, obtain, procure (by request or influence): si contendisset, impetraturum non fuisse, succeed: ab proximis, Cs.: ad impetr…

impetus.definition: impetus (inp-) ūs, m 1 in+PET-, an attack, assault, onset: armatorum: impetum facere in curiam, S.: ad regem, L.: hostes impetu facto nostros perturbaverunt, Cs.: impetum sustinere, Cs.: terrere eum impetu, S.: me in …

impexus.definition: impexus (in-p-) adj., uncombed: barbae, V.: porrigo, H.—Unpolished: antiquitas, Ta.

impie.definition: impiē (inp-) adv. impius, irreligiously, undutifully: in nos facere: deserere regem, Cu.

impietas.definition: impietās (inp-) ātis, f impius, irreverence, ungodliness, impiety, disloyalty: impietas et scelus: impietatis duces, treason: in parentem, S.: in deos inpietates.

impiger.definition: impiger (in-p-) gra, grum, adj., not indolent, diligent, active, quick, unwearied, indefatigable, energetic: mercator, H.: ingenium, S.: in scribendo: ad labores: militiā, L.: militiae, Ta.: hostium Vexare turmas, H.:…

impigre.definition: impigrē adv. impiger, actively, quickly, readily: hostium res attendere, S.: consulem sequi, L.

impigritas.definition: impigritās (inp-) ātis, f impiger, activity, indefatigableness.

impingo.definition: impingō (inp-) pēgī, pāctus, ere 1 in+pango, to dash against, throw on, thrust at, fasten upon: alcui lapidem, Ph.: uncus impactus est fugitivo illi: agmina muris, V.: hostes in vallum, Ta.: clitellas ferus impingas, …

impius.definition: impius (in-p-) adj., of persons, irreverent, ungodly, undutiful, unpatriotic, abandoned, wicked, impious: impium se esse fateri: Danaides, H.: miles, V.— As subst: has esse in impios poenas: numero impiorum haberi, Cs…

implacabilis.definition: implācābilis (inpl-) e, adj. 2 in+placabilis, unappeasable, implacable, irreconcilable: se mihi implacabilem praebere: Fabio, L.: numen, O.: iracundiae: ira, O.

implacabiliter.definition: (implācābiliter) adv., implacably.—Only comp: implacabilius irasci, Ta.

implacatus.definition: implācātus (in-pl-) adj., unappeased, insatiable: Charybdis, V.: gula, O.

implacidus.definition: 'implacidus (in-pl-) adj., ungentle, savage, fierce: genus, H.: fores, Pr.'

impleo.definition: impleō (in-pl-) ēvī (often implērunt, implēsse, etc., for implēvērunt, etc.), ētus, ēre PLE-, to fill up, fill full, make full, fill: libros: (harena) ora inplere solet, S.: frustis esculentis gremium suum: manum pinu…

implexus.definition: implexus P. in+plexus, interwoven, entwined: implexae crinibus anguī s Eumenides, V. —Involved: luctu continuo, Ta.

implicatio.definition: implicātiō (inpl-) ōnis, f implico, an interweaving: nervorum.— An insertion, incorporation: locorum communium.—An entangling, embarrassment: rei familiaris.

implicatus.definition: implicātus (inpl-) adj. P. of implico, entangled, involved, confused: nec in sermone quicquam: partes orationis.

implico.definition: implicō (in-pl-) āvī or uī, ātus or itus, ā re, to infold, involve, entangle, entwine, inwrap, envelop, encircle, embrace, clasp, grasp: incertos orbīs, V.: quam flumine curvo Implicuit Cephisos, O.: comam laevā, gras…

imploratio.definition: implōrātiō (inpl-) ōnis, f imploro, a call for help, imploring: deorum et hominum, upon gods, etc.: illius acerba.

imploro.definition: implōrō (in-pl-) āvī, ātus, āre in+ploro, to invoke with tears: nomen filii (i. e. filium nomine). —To call to help, call for aid, appeal to, invoke, beseech, entreat, implore: alqm: deos deasque omnīs: milites, ne, e…

implumis.definition: implūmis (inpl-) e, adj. 2 in+pluma, without feathers, unfledged, callow: pulli, H.: fetūs, V.

impluo.definition: impluō (in-p-) —, —, ere, to rain upon: summis adspergine silvis, O.

impluvium.definition: impluvium (inpl-) ī, n impluo, a small court open to the sky (forming the middle wall of a Roman house, and surrounded by covered galleries): Anguis in impluvium decidit de tegulis, T.: columnae ad impluvium.

impolitus.definition: impolītus (in-p-) adj., unpolished, rough, inelegant, unrefined: forma ingeni: res, i. e. unfinished: Timaeus compositione verborum.

impono.definition: impōnō (in-p-) posuī, positus (inpostus, V) ere, to place upon, set on, impose, establish, introduce, set, place: Metellum in rogum: In ignem impositast, fletur, T.: quo praesidium imposuerat, S.: eo mulieres imposuer…

importo.definition: importō (in-p-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bring in, introduce, bring from abroad, import: commeatūs in oppidum, Cs.: vinum ad se importari sinere, Cs.: aere utuntur importato, Cs.—Fig., to introduce, bring about, occasion, c…

importune.definition: importūnē (inp-) adv. importunus, unsuitably, rudely, violently: insistere.

importunitas.definition: importūnitās (inp-) ātis, f importunus, unsuitableness, unfitness: aniculae, T.—Unmannerliness, incivility, rudeness, insolence: molesta: homo incredibili importunitate: animi.

importunus.definition: importūnus (inp-) adj. with sup. 1 PER-, unfit, unsuitable, inconvenient: tempus: vi regere patriam inportunum est, S.: machinationibus locus, S.— Troublesome, grievous, distressing: pauperies, H.: Caphareus, stormy, …

importuosus.definition: importuōsus (inp-) adj. 2 in+portuosus, without a harbor: mare, S.: litora, L.

impotens.definition: impotēns (in-p-) entis, adj. with comp. and sup, powerless, impotent, weak, feeble, helpless: homo: ad opem: (Iuno) cesserat impotens Tellure, H.: gens rerum suarum, not master of, L.: regendi (sc. equos), unable to c…

impotenter.definition: (impotenter) adv. impotens, weakly, ineffectually.—Only comp: impotentius regi, L.

impotentia.definition: impotentia (inp-) ae, f impotens, helplessness, weakness: sua, T.— Ungovernableness, violence, fury, unbridled passion: animi: muliebris, L.: sine impotentiā, Ta.: astri aestuosa, fiery violence, H.

impraesentiarum.definition: impraesentiārum (inpr-) adv., for the present, under present circumstances, now: bellum componere, N.: quid conduceret, Ta.

impransus.definition: imprānsus (in-pr-) adj., that has not breakfasted, fasting: impransi mecum disquirite, H.: magister, H.

imprecor.definition: imprecor (in-pr-) ātus, ārī, to call down upon, imprecate: alcui diras, Ta.: Litora litoribus contraria, i. e. pronounce the curse of enmity upon, V.

impressio.definition: impressiō ōnis, f 1 in+PREM-, an onset, assault, attack, charge: in sinistrum cornu, L.: dant impressionem, L.—In rhythm, beats, C.— In speech, articulation: explanata vocum.—Fig., an impression, perception.

impressus2.definition: 'impressus (in-pr-) adj., unpressed, not milked: ubera, Pr.'

imprimis.definition: imprīmīs or in prīmīs see primus.

imprimo.definition: imprimō (inpr-) pressī, pressus, ere 1 in+ premo, to press upon, press against: Stamina impresso pollice nentes, O.: Impresso genu nitens, V.: inpressā tellurem reppulit hastā, i. e. raised herself, O.—To stamp, impri…

improbatio.definition: improbātiō (inpr-) ōnis, f improbo, disapproval, blame: ista omnis: hominis.

improbe.definition: improbē (inp-) adv. with comp. and sup. improbus, badly, wrongly, wickedly, recklessly: multa fecisti: dici: improbius fieri: quas (res) improbissime fecit: decerpere oscula, Ct.

improbitas.definition: improbitās (inpr-) ātis, f improbus, wickedness, depravity, dishonesty: singularis: calumniae: illo admirabilis aevo, i. e. rare, Iu.: simiae, roguishness.

improbo.definition: improbō (in-pr-) āvī, ātus, āre, to disapprove, blame, condemn, reject: qui si improbasset (SC.), Cs.: iudicium, overrule: per improbaturum haec Iovem, H.: potestas probandi improbandique (frumenti), rejecting: has (n…

improbulus.definition: improbulus (inpr-) adj. dim. improbus, somewhat wicked, a trifle impudent, Iu.

improbus.definition: improbus (in-pr-) adj. with comp. and sup, not good, bad, wicked, reprobate, abandoned, vile, base, impious, bold, shameless, wanton: nequam et improbus: longe post natos homines improbissimus: fugit improbus, the rog…

improcerus.definition: imprōcērus (in-pr-) adj., of small stature, undersized: pecora, Ta.

impromptus.definition: imprōmptus (in-pr-) adj., unready, hesitating: linguā, L.: Arminius, Ta.

improperatus.definition: improperātus (in-pr-) adj., not hasty, lingering: vestigia, V.

improsper.definition: imprōsper (in-p-) era, erum, adj., unfortunate, unprosperous: fortuna, Ta.: Claritudo generis, Ta.

improvide.definition: imprōvidē adv. improvidus, recklessly, improvidently: se in praeceps dare, L.

improvidus.definition: imprōvidus (in-p-) adj., not foreseeing, off guard: improvidos hostī s opprimere, L.: futuri certaminis, L.—Heedless, reckless, careless, regardless: senes: pectora, V.: festinatio improvida est, L.: consilii, Ta.: fu…

improviso.definition: imprōvīsō (in-p-) adv. improvisus, on a sudden, unexpectedly: pagum adoriri, Cs.: ut tempestates improviso concitantur: apparuit ignis, V.: repertus, O.

improvisus.definition: imprōvīsus (in-pr-) adj. with comp, not foreseen, unforeseen, unexpected: malum, S.: sapienti nihil improvisum accidere potest: pupilli calamitas: adventus: vis leti, H.: Improvisi aderunt, V.: anguis, concealed, V.: …

imprudens.definition: imprūdēns (in-pr-) entis, adj., not foreseeing, not expecting, without knowing, unaware, unsuspecting, ignorant, inconsiderate, heedless, inadvertent: dico omnia, T.: imprudentīs hostīs adgredi, Cs.: milites, off thei…

imprudenter.definition: imprūdenter (inpr-) adv. with comp. imprudens, without foresight, ignorantly, inconsiderately: putant: facere, N.: accessit imprudentius, T.

imprudentia.definition: imprūdentia (inpr-) ae, f imprudens, want of foresight, inconsiderateness, imprudence, ignorance, inadvertence: imprudentiā admissum facinus, S.: eventū s, L.: inprudentiā cursu decedere, Cs.: cum id imprudentiā accid…

impubes.definition: impūbēs (in-p-) eris (C., Cs., O.), and impūbis, is (H., V., L., O., Ta.), adj. 2 in+pubes, under age, youthful, beardless: filium impuberem necatum esse: servi omnes ad impuberes, Cs.: comes impubis Iuli, V.: impubem…

impudens.definition: impudēns (in-p-) entis, adj. with comp. and sup, without shame, shameless, impudent: pudens impudentem (fraudat): quis impudentior?: Impudens liqui patrios Penates, H.: audacia, T.: largitio, S.: furtum: impudentissim…

impudenter.definition: 'impudenter (inp-) adv. with comp. and sup. impudens, shamelessly, impudently: facere, T.: loqui: impudentius ab sociis abstulit: impudentissime mentiri.'

impudentia.definition: impudentia (inp-) ae, f impudens, shamelessness, impudence: quae perturbes haec tuā inpudentiā, T.: vicit tamen inpudentia, S.: inpudentiā fretus: tenere cuius inpudentiae est? Cs.

impudicitia.definition: impudīcitia ae, f impudicus, shamelessness, immodesty, impurity: sua.

impudicus.definition: impudīcus (in-p-) adj. with sup, shameless, impudent, without modesty: omnes impuri impudicique: et consul et impudicissimus: mulieres.

impugnatio.definition: impūgnātiō (inp-) ōnis, f impugno, an attack, assault.

impugno.definition: impūgnō (in-p-) āvī, ātus, āre, to fight against, attack, assail: acrius, Cs.: terga hostium, L.—To attack, assail, oppose, impugn: tempus impugnandi: acerrime regem, S.: nostra, H.

impulsio.definition: impulsiō (inp-) ōnis, f 1 in+1 PAL-, external pressure, influence: aliqua.—Fig., incitement, instigation, impulse: ad omnem animi motum: ad hilaritatem, pleasantry.

impulsor.definition: impulsor (inp-) ōris, m 1 in+1 PAL-, one who incites, an inciter, instigator: Syrus, T.: impulsores et socii sceleris illius: me inpulsore, T.

impulsus2.definition: impulsus (inp-) ūs, m 1 in+1 PAL-, a striking against, push, pressure, shock, impulse: impulsu scutorum copiae pulsae: alieno impulsu moveri: dimotis inpulsu pectoris undis, O.—Fig., incitement, instigation, influence…

impune.definition: impūne (inp-) adv. with comp. impunis, without punishment, unpunished, with impunity: haec facere, T.: facere (iniuriam) impune si possis: iniurias tulisse, inflicted, Cs.: occidi, unavenged: iniuriam accepisse, S.: a…

impunis.definition: impūnis (inp-) e, adj. 2 in+poena, unpunished: neve hoc inpune fuisset, O.: scelus, O.

impunitas.definition: impūnitās (inp-) ātis, f impunis, freedom from punishment, safety, impunity: illi inpunitatem concedere, S.: maximam inlecebram esse peccandi impunitatis spem: peccatorum.—Rashness, inconsiderateness: gladiorum: iuven…

impunite.definition: impūnītē adv. impunitus, with impunity: facere.

impunitus.definition: impūnītus (in-p-) adj. with comp, unpunished, unrestrained, free from danger, safe, secure: iniuria: scelus, S.: nec diu proditoribus impunita res fuit, L.: qui tu impunitior illa obsonia captas? H.: quo inpunitior si…

impuratus.definition: impūrātus (inp-) adj. impurus, defiled, infamous, abandoned, vile: ille, that vile wretch, T.: hunc inpuratum Ulcisci, T.

impure.definition: impūrē adv. with sup. impurus, basely, shamefully, vilely, infamously: impure atque flagitiose vivere: a quo impurissime haec nostra fortuna despecta est.

impuritas.definition: impūritās (inp-) ātis, f impurus, uncleanness, pollution, impurity: caeni: omnīs impuritates suscipere.

impurus.definition: impūrus (inp-) adj. with comp. and sup. 2 in+purus, unclean, filthy, foul: impurae matris prolapsus ab alvo, O.—Fig., unclean, defiled, impure, infamous, abandoned, vile: vox: historia, O.: animus, S.: persona: O homi…

imputatus2.definition: imputātus (inp-) adj. 2 in+putatus, unpruned, untrimmed: vinea, H.

imputo.definition: imputō (inp-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 in+puto, to reckon, attribute, make account of, charge, ascribe, impute: data (munera), Ta.: beneficium mihi, Ph.: natum imputat illis, (the fate of) his son, O.: exercitui moras belli, Ta.

imulus.definition: īmulus adj. dim. imus, the lowest: auricilla, Ct.

imus.definition: īmus adj. sup. contr. for infimus, the lowest, deepest, last: ab imis unguibus usque ad verticem summum: penetralia, O.: imā verrit vestigia caudā , tip, V.: fundo in imo, at the very bottom, V.: vox, the highest treb…

in.definition: in old indu, prep. with acc. or abl. I. With acc., in space, with verbs implying entrance, into, to: in Epirum venire: in flumen deicere: in Ubios legatos mittere, Cs.: Thalam pervenit, in oppidum magnum, S.—Fig.: in …

in-.definition: in- an inseparable particle cf. Gr. a)-, a)n-; Germ. and Eng. un-, which, prefixed to an adj., negatives or reverses the meaning: impar, unequal: intolerabilis, unbearable: immitis, ruthless. —In tmesis: Hanc . . . In…

inaccessus.definition: 'in-accessus adj., unapproached, inaccessible: lucus, V.: spelunca radiis, V.'

inacesco.definition: in-acēscō —, —, ere, inch, to turn sour at, sour upon.— Fig.: tibi per sensūs, i. e. imbitter you, O.

inaedifico.definition: in-aedificō āvī, ātus, āre, to build as a superstructure, erect as an addition, erect, construct: inaedificata in muris moenia, Cs.: in quā (domo) sacellum: quae in loca publica inaedificata habebant, L.— To build up,…

inaequabilis.definition: in-aequābilis e, adj., uneven, unequal: solum, L.: varietas.

inaequalis.definition: in-aequālis e, adj., uneven: loca, Ta.: phiala, Iu.—Unequal, unlike: portūs, of different sizes, O.: calices, H.: autumni, changeable, O.: Vixit inaequalis, clavum ut mutaret in horas, inconstant, H.: tonsor, that cut…

inaequaliter.definition: inaequāliter adv. inaequalis, unequally, disproportionately: deprimere alios, alios extollere, L.: campus sinuatur, Ta.

inaequo.definition: in-aequō —, —, āre, to make even, level: haec cratibus terrāque, Cs.

inaestimabilis.definition: in-aestimābilis e, adj., not to be judged of, unaccountable: animi multitudinis, L.—Inestimable, invaluable, incalculable: e grege se velut inaestimabilem secernere, L.: gaudium, L.—Not estimable, valueless.

inaestuo.definition: in-aestuō —, —, āre, to boil in, rage within: inaestuat praecordiis bilis, H.

inamabilis.definition: in-amābilis e, adj., unlovely, unattractive, repugnant, repulsive, odious: palus undā, i. e. the Styx, V.: regnum (of Pluto), O.

inamaresco.definition: in-amārēscō —, —, ere, inch, to become bitter: epulae, H.

inambitiosus.definition: in-ambitiōsus adj., unambitious, modest: rura, O.

inambulatio.definition: inambulātiō ōnis, f inambulo, a walking up and down, C.—A shaking, swaying: lecti, Ct.

inambulo.definition: in-ambulō —, —, āre, to walk up and down, pace to and fro: ante lucem domi; in porticu: per muros, L.

inamoenus.definition: 'in-amoenus adj., unpleasant, disagreeable, gloomy: regna (of Pluto), O.'

inane.definition: ināne is, n inanis, an empty space, void, open space: ad inane pervenire, L.: nullum: vacuum, V.: audito sonitu per inane, O.: rapti per inania vento, O.— Fig., vanity, worthlessness: inane abscindere soldo, H.: inani…

inanimalis.definition: in-animālis e, adj., without life, inanimate: animalia inanimaliaque omnia, L. (al. inanima).

inanimus.definition: 'inanimus adj. 2 in+anima, lifeless, inanimate: inanimum est omne, quod, etc.: natura.'

inanis.definition: inānis e, adj. with comp. and sup, empty, void: vas: domum reddere inanem: naves (opp. onustae), Cs.: naves, dismantled: tumulus, cenotaph, V.: sepulchrum, O.—Void, stripped, deserted, abandoned, unoccupied: civitas: …

inanitas.definition: inānitās ātis, f inanis, emptiness, empty space: per inanitatem ferri.—Fig., worthlessness. inanity: summa.

inaniter.definition: ināniter adv. inanis, vainly, idly, uselessly: exsultare: pectus angere, H.

inaratus.definition: in-arātus adj., unploughed, untilled, fallow: terra, V.: tellus, H.

inardesco.definition: in-ārdēscō ārsī, —, ere, inch, to kindle, take fire, burn, glow: nubes Solis inardescit radiis, V.: aestuosius, H.— Fig.: amor specie praesentis inarsit, O.: cupidine vindictae, Ta.

inattenuatus.definition: in-attenuātus adj., undiminished: fames, unappeased, O.

inaudax.definition: in-audāx ācis, adj., not daring, timorous: raptor, H.

inaudio.definition: in-audiō īvī, ītus, īre, to hear whispered, get an inkling of: re Gadibus inauditā fore ut, etc., it having been rumored among, etc.: numquid de quo inaudisti?

inauditus.definition: in-audītus adj., unheard-of, unusual, strange, new, incredible: agger novi generis atque inauditus, Cs.: scelus: incredibilis atque inaudita gravitas: cui sunt inauditae querellae tuae?: volucres, Ta.—Unheard, not bro…

inaugurato.definition: inaugurātō adv. (P. of inauguro, abl absol.), after taking auguries, with regard to omens: id inaugurato facere, L.: consecrare locum, L.

inauguro.definition: in-augurō āvī, ātus, āre, to take omens from the flight of birds, practise augury, divine: ad inaugurandum templa capiunt, L.: divine tu, inaugura, fierine possit, L.—To hallow by augury, consecrate, inaugurate, insta…

inauratus.definition: inaurātus adj. P. of inauro, gilded, golden: statua: quem inauratum in Capitolio fuisse, etc. (i. e. cuius statuam): acanthus, O.: Hercules, Iu.

inauro.definition: in-aurō —, ātus, āre, to overlay with gold.— Fig., to gild, enrich: a Caesare inaurari: ut te liquidus fortunae rivus inauret, H.

inauspicato.definition: in-auspicātō adv. inauspicatus, without consulting the auspices: pomoerium transgredi.

inauspicatus.definition: in-auspicātus adj., without consulting the auspices: lex, passed without omens, L.

inausus.definition: 'in-ausus adj., not ventured, unattempted: nil linquere inausum, V.: quid inausum vobis? Ta.'

incaeduus.definition: 'in-caeduus adj., uncut, not felled: lucus, O.'

incalesco.definition: in-calēscō caluī, —, ere, inch, to grow warm, be heated, glow: incalescente sole, L.: incaluit vis illa mali (i. e. veneni), O.: vino, L.—Fig., to glow, kindle, be inspired: deo, O.: acres Incaluere animi (equorum), O…

incalfacio.definition: in-calfaciō —, —, ere, to warm, heat: culmos Titan incalfacit, O.: cultros, O.

incallide.definition: incallidē adv. incallidus, unskilfully: non incallide, cleverly.

incallidus.definition: 'in-callidus adj., unskilful, unintelligent: servus non incallidus: homines.'

incandesco.definition: in-candēscō duī, —, inch, to grow warm, be heated, glow, kindle: illud (plumbum) incandescit eundo, O.: spumis incanduit unda, Ct.: Tempestas autumni incanduit aestu, V.

incanesco.definition: (in-cānēscō) canuī, —, ere, inch, to become white, turn gray, grow hoary (only perf.): ornusque incanuit albo Flore piri, V.

incanto.definition: in-cantō —, ātus, āre, to enchant, fix a spell upon: incantata vincula, love-charms, H.

incanus.definition: in-cānus adj., gray, hoary: menta, V.: labra Famis, pallid, O.: saecula, hoary centuries, Ct.

incassum.definition: 'in-cassum or in cassum adv. see cassus, in vain, to no purpose, uselessly: furere, V.: tot pati labores, V.: missae preces, L.: studio gestire lavandi, wantonly, V.'

incaute.definition: incautē adv. with comp. incautus, incautiously, inconsiderately, recklessly: stulte omnia et incaute: pugnare, L.: incautius custodiae dispositae, Cs.: murum incautius subit, L.

incautus.definition: in-cautus adj. with comp, incautious, improvident, inconsiderate, heedless, reckless: homo: in ipsum incautum incidere, Cs.: ab secundis rebus incauti, L.: ad credendum pavor, L.: studio eundi, O.: morte sodalis, made…

incedo.definition: in-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere, to advance, march, proceed, stride, move, stalk, strut: Virum incedere Video, T.: socios per ipsos, V.: Per meos finī s, H.: totā in urbe, O.: quācumque incederet: si pedes incedat, on foot…

incelebratus.definition: in-celebrātus adj., not spread abroad, Ta.

incendiarius.definition: incendiārius ī, m incendium, an incendiary, Ta.

incendium.definition: incendium ī, n in+CAND-, a burning, fire, conflagration: calamitosum, S.: in incendiis faciendis, Cs.: frumentum flumine atque incendio conruperunt, Cs.: nihil cogitant nisi incendia: neglecta solent incendia sumere v…

incendo.definition: incendō dī, sus, ere CAND-, to set fire to, kindle, burn: cupas taedā ac pice refertas, Cs.: odoribus incensis: lychnos, V.: urbem, S.: aedificia vicosque, Cs.: navīs: aedīs, Iu.: vepres, V.: cum ipse circumsessus pae…

incensio.definition: incēnsiō ōnis, f 1 in+CAND-, a setting on fire, burning: Capitoli: incensione urbem liberavi.

incensus1.definition: incēnsus adj. P. of incendo, inflamed, fiery, hot: incensos aestū s avertere, V.: in meditando.

incensus2.definition: incēnsus adj. 2 in+census, not assessed, unregistered: hominem incensum vendere: populus, L.—Plur m. as subst: lex de incensis lata, L.

inceptio.definition: inceptiō ōnis, f 1 in+CAP-, a beginning, undertaking: tam praeclari operis.—An enterprise, undertaking: est amentium, non amantium, T.

incepto.definition: inceptō —, —, āre, freq. incipio, to begin, attempt: fabulam, T.—To begin, get into a quarrel: cum illo homine, T.

inceptor.definition: inceptor ōris, m 1 in+CAP-, a beginner: mearum voluptatum, T.

inceptum.definition: inceptum ī, n P. neut. of incipio, a beginning: incepta gravia, H.— An attempt, undertaking: illud, T.: contra patriam: a quo incepto me detinere, S.: cuius neque inceptum ullum frustra erat, S.: absistere incepto, L.…

inceptus2.definition: (inceptus, ūs) m 1 in+CAP-, a beginning, undertaking (only abl sing.): turpe inceptūst, T.: foedum inceptu, foedum exitu, L.

incerno.definition: (in-cernō) —, crētus, ere, to sift in, add with a sieve.— Only P. perf.: piper album incretum, H.

incero.definition: in-cērō —, ātus, āre, to cover with wax: genua deorum (i. e. with wax votive tablets), Iu.

incertum1.definition: incertum ī, n incertus, an uncertainty: ne cuius incerti vanique auctor esset, L.: scribere legiones ad incerta belli, contingencies, L.: Haud incerta cano, V.: bona omnium in dubium incertumque revocabuntur: praefect…

incertum2.definition: 'incertum adv. neut. of incertus, doubtfully: vigilans, half awake, O.'

indetonsus.definition: in-dētōnsus adj., with unshorn hair, O.

indevitatus.definition: in-dēvītātus adj., unavoided, sure: telum, O.

index.definition: index dicis, m and f in+DIC-, one who points out, a discloser, discoverer, informer, witness: falsus, S.: haec omnia indices detulerunt.— An informer, betrayer, spy: vallatus indicibus: saeptus armatis indicibus: sile…

indicens.definition: in-dīcēns entis, adj., that does not say: Non me indicente haec fiunt, not without my telling, T.: me indicente, L.

indicium.definition: indicium ī, n 1 in+DIC-, a notice, information, discovery, disclosure, charge, evidence: id anus mihi indicium fecit, T.: falsum, S.: crimen indicio Avilli comprobabatur: res per indicium enuntiata, Cs.: indicii poena…

indico1.definition: indicō āvī, ātus, āre index, to point out, indicate, inform, show, declare, disclose, make known, reveal, betray: de coniuratione, S.: causam pestis, L.: indicatis deprehensisque internuntiis, Cs.: aliquid in volgus, …

indico2.definition: in-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to declare publicly, proclaim, publish, announce, appoint: concilium in diem certam, Cs.: forum, V.: ieiunia, H.: dies indicta pugnae, L.: funus ut indicatur, that invitations be issued: div…

indictus2.definition: in-dictus adj., not said, unsaid: Quod dic tum, indictumst, T.: ea ut indicta sint, revocare L.: carminibus nostris indictus, unsung, V.: in signe, adhuc Indictum ore alio, H.: indictā causā interfecti, without a hear…

indidem.definition: indidem adv. inde, from the same place. quos homines? indidemne Ameriā an ex urbe?: Thebis, likewise from Thebes, N.: additi erant Bruttiorum indidem perfugae, also from Sicily, L. —From the same thing, from the same …

indifferens.definition: in-differēns entis, adj., not to be sought or shunned, indifferent, neither good nor evil.

indigena.definition: indigena ae, adj. indu+GEN-, sprung from the land, native, indigenous: miles, L.: Fauni Nymphaeque, V.: apri, O.—As subst m., a native, son of the soil: maiores eorum, L.: hoc indigenae vivebant more, aborigines, Iu.

indigens.definition: indigēns ntis, adj. P. of indigeo, in want of, needing: mei: alienarum opum, N.—Plur. as subst: indigentibus benigne facere, the poor.

indigentia.definition: indigentia ae, f indigens, need, want, indigence: ab indigentiā orta amicitia.—Insatiableness, insatiable desire: est libido inexplebilis.

indigeo.definition: indigeō uī,—, ēre indu+egeo, to need, want, stand in need of, demand, require: bonā existimatione: pecuniā, N.: rebus, quae ad oppugnationem sunt usui, Cs.: huius patris, T.: bellum indiget celeritatis: quorum indiget…

indiges2.definition: indigēs is, adj. indu+EG-, needy, indigent, Pac. ap. C.

indigestus.definition: in-dīgestus adj., unorganized, without order, confused: moles, O.

indignabundus.definition: indīgnābundus adj. indignor, full of indignation, enraged: muliebriter, L.

indignandus.definition: indīgnandus adj. P. of indignor, to be despised, deserving contempt: (vestis) lecto, O.

indignans.definition: indīgnāns antis, adj. P. of indignor, impatient, reluctant, indignant: venti, V.: ursi, O.

indignatio.definition: indīgnātiō ōnis, f indignor, displeasure, indignation, disdain: liberrima, H.: indignationem movere, L.: publicae, expressions of indignation, L.—In rhet., an appeal exciting indignation.— A provocation, occasion for …

indignatus.definition: indīgnātus adj. P. of indignor, angered, reluctant: Vita fugit sub umbras, V.

indigne.definition: indīgnē adv. with comp. and sup. indignus, unworthily, undeservedly, dishonorably, shamefully: Facis iniuriam illi, T.: indignius obtrectatum esse, ne, etc.: indignissime interire, Cs.—Angrily, indignantly: neque indi…

indignitas.definition: indīgnitās ātis, f indignus, unworthiness, vileness, shamefulness: propter indignitatem repudiatus: rei, Cs.—Unworthy conduct, insult, indignity, outrage, baseness: Omnīs indignitates perferre, Cs.: inpensius iis indi…

indignor.definition: in-dīgnor ātus, ārī, dep. indignus, to deem unworthy, be indignant, despise, resent, be offended: ea, quae indignentur adversarii: suam vicem, L.: pontem indignatus Araxes, disdaining to bear, V.: indignantes milites,…

indignus.definition: in-dīgnus adj. with comp. and sup, unworthy, undeserving, unfit: senator voluerat fieri, quamvis indignus: indignissimi candidati, L.: poëta, incompetent, H.: te omni honore indignissimum iudicat: magnorum avorum, V.:…

indigus.definition: 'indigus adj. 1 in+EG-, needing, in want: nullius, S.: nostrae opis, V.'

indiligens.definition: in-dīligēns tis, adj. with comp, careless, heedless, negligent: nimium, T.: pater familias, N.: si indiligentiores fuerint, Cs.

indiligenter.definition: indīligenter adv. with comp. indiligens, carelessly, heedlessly, negligently: nihil ab eo (factum): praesidia indiligentius servare, Cs.

indiligentia.definition: indīligentia ae, f indiligens, carelessness, heedlessness, negligence: litterarum missarum: Aeduorum, Cs.

indipiscor.definition: indipīscor eptus, ī, dep. indu+apiscor, to obtain, attain, reach, seize: navem, L.

indiscretus.definition: in-discrētus adj., undistinguishable, not known apart: proles suis, V.: voces, confused, Ta.

indisertus.definition: 'in-disertus adj., not eloquent: Academicus: prudentia, at a loss for words.'

indispositus.definition: 'in-dispositus adj., without order, confused: Apud Vitellium omnia, Ta.'

indistinctus.definition: 'in-distinctus adj., undistinguished, confused: corollae, Ct.: defensio, Ta.'

inditus.definition: 'inditus adj. P. of indo, put on, laid on, imposed. vincula, Ta.: custodes, Ta.'

individuum.definition: indīviduum ī, n individuus, an atom, indivisible particle.

indo.definition: indō didī, ditus, ere 1 in+do, to put into, insert: digitos (in the thongs of the javelin), O.: venenum potioni, Cu.: novos ritūs, to introduce, Ta. —Fig., of a name, to give, apply, confer: artificibus . . . nomen hi…

indocilis.definition: in-docilis e, adj., not teachable, not to be taught, indocile: nimis: collum (tigrium), tameless, H.: pauperiem pati, H.—Untaught, unlearned, ignorant: genus, V.: viae, Pr.—Unpolished, rude: Indocili numero mollit opu…

indocte.definition: in-doctē adv. indoctus, unlearnedly, unskilfully: facere.

indoctus.definition: in-doctus adj. with comp, untaught, unlearned, uninstructed, ignorant, unskilful: multitudo: habitus indoctior: Cantabrum indoctum iuga ferre nostra, H.: pilae discive trochive, H.— Neut. adverb: canet indoctum, witho…

indolentia.definition: indolentia ae, f in-dolens (2 in-), freedom from pain, insensibility.

indoles.definition: indolēs is, f indu+1 OL-, an inborn quality, natural quality, nature: in frugibus pecudibusque, L.—Native quality, nature, character, genius, disposition: adulescentes bonā indole praediti: virtutum atque vitiorum, L.…

indolesco.definition: indolēscō luī, —, ere * in-doleo, to feel pain, smart, ache, be grieved, be distressed: indolui, O.: qui non indoluerit: successurumque Minervae indoluit, O.: malis, O.: id ipsum indoluit Iuno, O.

indomitus.definition: in-domitus adj., untamed, ungovernable, wild: equus, H.: indomitā cervice feri, H.—Unsubdued, unrestrained, indomitable: pastores, Cs.: agricolae, V.: dextra, unconquered, O.—Fig., unrestrained, unbridled, indomitable…

indormio.definition: in-dormiō īvī, ītus, īre, to fall asleep on, sleep upon: congestis undique saccis Indormis, H.: Indormit unctis cubilibus, H.— Fig., to sleep over, do negligently, be careless about: in isto homine colendo: tantae cau…

indotatus.definition: in-dōtātus adj., unportioned, portionless: (virgo), T.: soror, H.—Fig., unadorned, poor: ars.— Poet.: corpora, without funeral honors, O.

indu.definition: indu old for 1 in; see indipiscor, indoles, induperator, industrius, indutiae.

indubito.definition: in-dubitō —, —, āre, to throw doubt upon, express distrust of: Viribus tuis, V.

indubius.definition: 'in-dubius adj., not doubtful, certain: innocentia, Ta.'

induco.definition: in-dūcō dūxī (indūxtī for indūxī stī, T.), ductus, ere, to lead in, bring in, introduce, conduct, lead up, bring forward: metuens induceris (i. e. in domum), H.: legionis principes (sc. in urbem), L.: turmas inducit A…

inductio.definition: inductiō ōnis, f 1 in+DVC-, a bringing in, introducing, production, admission: aquarum inductiones: horum (iuvenum in circum), for exhibition, L.— Fig., a purpose, resolution, determination: animi.—An inclination, lea…

indulgens.definition: indulgēns entis, adj. with comp. P. of indulgeo, indulgent, kind, tender, fond: nomen indulgentius maternum: ministri irarum, L.: obsequium peccatis indulgens: sibi hydrops, H.: civitas in captivos, L.

indulgenter.definition: 'indulgenter adv. indulgens, indulgently, kindly, tenderly: loqui: bestiae multa faciunt.'

indulgentia.definition: indulgentia ae, f indulgens, a yielding, indulgence, forbearance: Caesaris in se, Cs.: mea in illum (conlegam): corporis.—Tenderness, fondness, affection, favor: patria: in huius (matris) indulgentiā educatus, Ta.: Ca…

indulgeo.definition: indulgeō ulsī, ultus, ēre, to be complaisant, be kind, be tender, exercise forbearance, incline, yield, indulge, concede, grant, allow: Hactenus indulsisse vacat, thus far then I can yield, V.: Aeduorum civitati, Cs.:…

induo.definition: induō uī, ūtus, ere indu+4 AV-, to put on, assume, dress in: Meam (vestem), T.: vestes Indutae, V.: lugubria, O.: Herculi tunicam: galeas, Cs.: albos crinīs, V.: scalas, shouldered, O.: raptae insignia Bacchi, O.: sib…

induperator.definition: induperātor ōris, m indupero, old for impero, a commander-in-chief, emperor: barbarus, Iu.

induratus.definition: indūrātus adj. P. of induro, hardened.— Fig.: induratus resistendo hostium timor, L.

induresco.definition: in-dūrēscō uī, —, ere, inch, to grow hard on, stiffen upon: Stiria inpexis induruit barbis, V.: saxo induruit tumor, to stone, O.—Fig.: miles induruerat pro Vitellio, had become firmly attached, Ta.

induro.definition: in-dūrō —, —, āre, to make hard, harden: nivī s, O.: ora cornu Indurata, O.

industria.definition: industria ae, f industrius, diligence, activity, assiduity, industry, zeal: poëtae ad scribendum, T.: ingenium industriā alitur: naturam industriā vincere, S.: in scribendo tantum industriae ponam, pains: magna, N.: i…

industrius.definition: 'industrius adj. indu+STRV-, active, diligent, assiduous, industrious: primo industrios esse, deinde, etc., S.: homo: in rebus gerundis: armis, Iu.'

indutiae.definition: indūtiae (not -ūciae), ārum, f indu+1 I-, a suspension of hostitities, truce, armistice: dies indutiis petitus, Cs.: triginta dierum cum hoste pactae: indutias facere: tollere, put an end to, L.: agitare, S.: per indu…

indutus2.definition: (indūtus ūs), m a putting on.—Only dat: quam (vestem) indutui gerebat, Ta.

inebrio.definition: in-ēbriō —, —, āre, to make drunk, intoxicate: miseram aurem, drench, Iu.

inedia.definition: inedia ae, f 2 in+ED-, an abstaining from food, fasting: inediae patiens, S.: fessus inediā.

ineditus.definition: in-ēditus adj., not made known, unknown: cura, O.

inelegans.definition: in-ēlegāns antis, adj., not choice, inelegant: orationis copia.

ineleganter.definition: inēleganter adv. inelegans, not choicely, inelegantly: scribere: dividere, illogically.

ineluctabilis.definition: in-ēlūctābilis e, adj., not to be escuped, inevitable: tempus, V.: fatum, V.

inemorior.definition: in-ēmorior —, ī, to die upon: dapis spectaculo, to starve in sight of a feast, H.

inemptus.definition: in-ēmptus (inēmtus) adj., unbought, unpurchased: dapes, V.: corpus inemptum Reddito, without a ransom, O.: consulatus, Ta.

inenarrabilis.definition: in-ēnārrābilis e, adj., indescribable: labor, L.

ineo.definition: in-eō īvī and iī, itus, īre, to go into, enter: illius domum: urbem, L.: viam, begin a journey: ineunt proscaenia ludi, come on the stage, V.: nemus nullis illud initur equis, O.: in urbem, L.— Fig., to come in, make …

inepte.definition: ineptē adv. ineptus, improperly, impertinently, absurdly: disserere: dicere: nil molitur inepte, H.: fautor (i. e. favens), H.

ineptia.definition: ineptia ae, f ineptus, silliness, folly, absurdity: tua, T.—Plur, silliness, fooleries, trifles, absurdities: omnium ineptiarum an ulla sit maior, quam, etc.: paene aniles: mearum ineptiarum lectores, Ct.

ineptio.definition: ineptiō —, —, īre ineptia, to be absurd, trifle, play the fool: ineptis, T.: desinas ineptire, Ct.

ineptus.definition: ineptus adj. with comp. 2 in+aptus.—Of persons, absurd, awkward, silly, inept, impertinent: Quid est, inepta, quid vis? T.: ineptus Et iactantior hic paulo est, without tact, H.—Of things, absurd, unsuitable, unfit, i…

inequitabilis.definition: in-equitābilis e, adj., unfit for riding over, impassable to horsemen: campi, Cu.

inermis.definition: inermis e, adj. 2 in+arma, unarmed, without weapons, defenceless: tribunus: milites, Cs.: latrones, S.: inermis Constitit, V.: ex agro inermi ac nudo praesidiis, L.: me lupus Fugit inermem, H.: bracchia, O.: gingiva, …

inermus.definition: 'inermus adj. 2 in+arma, unarmed, without weapons: alquos inermos timere, Cs.: pectus, V.: cum paucis inermis.'

inerrans.definition: in-errāns tis, adj., not wandering, fixed: stellae.

inerro.definition: in-errō —, —, āre, to wander, err: si versus noster summo inerret in ore, i. e. is repeated inaccurately, Tb.

iners.definition: iners ertis, adj. with comp. and sup. 2 in+ars, without skill, unskilful, incompetent: artes, quibus qui carebant, inertes nominabantur: scriptor, H.: superando inertīs, O.: homo non inertissimus.— Helpless, weak, ina…

inertia.definition: inertia ae, f iners, want of art, unskilfulness, ignorance, rudeness: adfecti artibus, inertiis. —Inactivity, idleness, laziness: animi, S.: turpis: hominum: laboris, aversion to: operis, L.: strenua, H.

ineruditus.definition: in-ērudītus adj., unlearned, illiterate: Epicurus.—Crude, inconsiderate: illud tam ineruditum respondere.

inesco.definition: inēscō āvī, ātus, āre 1 in+esca, to allure with bait, entice: velut inescatam temeritatem consulis, L.—Fig., to entice, deceive: homines, T.: specie benefici inescamur, L.

inevitabilis.definition: in-ēvītābilis e, adj., unavoidable, inevitable: fulmen, O.: fatum, Cu.: crimen, Ta.

inexcitus.definition: in-excītus adj., unmoved, calm: Ausonia, V.

inexcusabilis.definition: in-excūsābilis e, adj., without excuse: (tu), H.: tempus, affording no excuse, O.

inexercitatus.definition: in-exercitātus adj., untrained, unskilful, without experience: miles: copiae, N.

inexhaustus.definition: 'in-exhaustus adj., not wasted: pubertas, not enfeebled, Ta.: metalla, inexhaustible, V.'

inexorabilis.definition: in-exōrābilis e, adj., not to be moved by entreaty, unyielding, inexorable: ingenium, T.: iudices: Achilles, H.: in ceteros: adversus te, L.: leges rem inexorabilem esse, L.: odium, O.: fatum, V.

inexpeditus.definition: (in-expedītus) adj., not free, entangled, confused.—Only comp: pugna inexpeditior, L.

inexpertus.definition: in-expertus adj., without experience, unpractised: exercitus bonis inexpertus, L.: animus ad contumeliam, L.: Dulcis inexpertis, H.—Untried, unproved, untested: fides, L.: legiones, Ta.: Ne quid inexpertum relinquat, …

inexpiabilis.definition: in-expiābilis e, adj., not to be atoned for, inexpiable: religiones: scelus.—Implacable, irreconcilable, obstinate: se mihi inexpiabilem praebere: odium, L.: bellum.

inexplebilis.definition: in-explēbilis e, adj., not to be satisfied, insatiable: populi fauces: cupiditas: vir virtutis, L.

inexpletus.definition: in-explētus adj., not filled, unsatisfied: lumen, eye, O.: inexpletus lacrimans, incessantly, V.

inexplicabilis.definition: in-explicābilis e, adj., not to be loosened, inextricable, intricate: vinculum, Cu.—Obstructed, not to be traversed: viae imbribus, L.—Fig., inexplicable: o rem inexplicabilem!: facilitas, i. e. with no result, L.

inexplorato.definition: inexplōrātō adv. abl. of inexploratus, without previous examination: profectus, L.: angustiis superatis, L.

inexploratus.definition: in-explōrātus adj., unexplored, unknown: vada, L.

inexpugnabilis.definition: in-expūgnābilis e, adj., not to be stormed, impregnable: arx, L.: gramen, not to be rooted out, O.: pectus Amori, invincible, O.: via, impassable, L.—Fig., unassailable: alqs.

inexspectatus.definition: in-exspectātus (inexp-) adj., unlooked for: in armis Hostis adest, O.: vis.

inexstinctus.definition: 'in-exstinctus adj., unextinguished, unextinguishable: ignis, O.: nomen, imperishable, O.: libido, insatiable, O.'

inexsuperabilis.definition: in-exsuperābilis (inexup-) e, adj. with comp, not to be crossed, insurmountable: Alpes, L.: ripa, L.: inexsuperabilior saltus, L.—Fig.: vis fati, invincible, L.—Plur n. as subst: inexsuperabilibus vim adferre, overcom…

inextricabilis.definition: in-extrīcābilis e, adj., not to be unravelled, inextricable: error (of the labyrinth), V.

infabre.definition: īn-fabrē adv., unskilfully, rudely: vasa non infabre facta, L.: sculptum, H.

infabricatus.definition: īn-fabricātus adj., unwrought, unfashioned: robora, V.

infacetiae.definition: īnfacētiae (infic-) ārum, f coarse jokes, tasteless attempts at wit, Ct.

infacetus.definition: īn-facētus (infic-) adj. with comp, without wit, dull, stupid: nec infacetus: non inficetum mendacium: Idem infaceto est infacetior rure, Ct.

infacundus.definition: īn-fācundus adj. with comp, not eloquent: vir, L.: infacundior, slow of speech, L.

infamatus.definition: īnfamātus adj. P. of infamo, of ill repute: dea, O.

infamia.definition: īnfāmia ae, f infamis, ill fame, ill report, bad repute, dishonor, disgrace, infamy: rei, Cs.: ne infamiae Ea res sibi esset, T.: indicia operta infamiā: mendax, calumny, H.: infamiam ferre: infamiā aspergi, N.: se er…

infamis.definition: īnfāmis e, adj. 2 in + fama, of ill repute, disreputable, notorious, infamous: mulier: auctor deserendae Italiae, L.: scopuli, H.: flagitiis infamem fieri, T.: homines omni dedecore: captarum pecuniarum suspicione, L.…

infamo.definition: īnfāmō āvī, ātus, āre infamis, to bring into ill repute, disgrace, dishonor, defame: aliorum iniuriam: hunc infamatum, branded, N.: infamandae rei causā, of making notorious, L.

infandus.definition: īn-fandus adj., unspeakable, unutterable, unheard of, unnatural, shocking, abominable: facinus, T.: res: epulae, i. e. of human flesh, L.: amor, V.: bellum, V.: stuprum, L.—Plur n. as subst: infanda furens, V.—Sing n.…

infans.definition: īnfāns fantis, adj. with comp. and sup. 2 in + for, that cannot speak, without speech, mute, speechless: statuae, H.: filium, cum infans esset, locutum.—Poor of speech, not eloquent: homines: pudor, i. e. embarrassmen…

infantia.definition: īnfantia ae, f infans, inability to speak, want of eloquence: incredibilis.— Childhood: nostra, Iu. —Second childhood, childishness: madidi nasi, Iu.

infatuo.definition: īnfatuō —, —, āre * in-fatuus, to make a fool of, infatuate: hominem mercede: neminem.

infaustus.definition: īn-faustus adj., of ill omen, unfortunate, unpropitious: puppes, V.: gradus, O.: dies, Ta.— Of persons, unfortunate: bellis, Ta.

infector.definition: īnfector ōris, m 2 FAC-, a dyer.

infectus1.definition: īnfectus adj. 2 in+factus, not done, unwrought, unmade, undone, unaccomplished, unfinished: pro infecto haberi: omnia pro infecto sint, be regarded, L.: infectum reddet quod, etc., undo, H.: infectā pace dimissi, with…

infecunditas.definition: īnfēcunditās ātis, f infecundus, unfruitfulness: terrarum, Ta.

infecundus.definition: īn-fēcundus adj., unfruitful: ager arbore, S.: Sponte suā quae se tollunt . . . Infecunda, V.

infelicitas.definition: īnfēlīcitās ātis, f infelix, ill-luck, misfortune: quid hoc infelicitatis? T.: tua: gravior, L.

infeliciter.definition: īnfēlīciter adv. infelix, unhappily, unfortunately: fit mihi obviam, T.: tentata res, L.

infelix.definition: īn-fēlīx īcis, adj. with comp. and sup, unfruitful, not fertile, barren: lolium, V.: tellus frugibus, V.: foliis oleaster, V.: arbori infelici suspendere, hang on the accursed tree, hang, crucify, L.— Unfortunate, ill…

infense.definition: (īnfēnsē) adv. infensus, with hostility, bitterly: invectus, Ta.: Isocrati adversatus infensius: infensius pugnare, L.

infenso.definition: īnfēnsō —, —, āre infensus, to treat in a hostile manner, ravage: bello Armeniam, Ta.—To be hostile: quasi infensantibus Dis, Ta.

infensus.definition: īnfēnsus adj. with comp. FEN-, hostile, inimical, enraged: Me infensus servat, T.: infenso animo venire: ignis, V.: mentes mihi: Drances Turno, V.: infensioribus in se quam in illum iudicibus, L.: ad infensius serviti…

infercio.definition: īnferciō —, —, īre 1 in+farcio, to stuff in, force in: inferciens verba.

inferiae.definition: īnferiae ārum, f plur. inferus, sacrifices in honor of the dead: Inferiae cadunt cineri, O.: cui inferias adferunt: Absenti ferat inferias, V.: nepotes Rettulit inferias Iugurthae, H.: mānibus dare, O.

inferior.definition: īnferior ius, adj. comp. of inferus, lower, further down: spatium, Cs.: locus (opp. superior): in inferius ferri, downwards, O.: Africae pars, i. e. nearer the sea, S.: caelum sidet inferius mari, H.: effigies, smalle…

inferius.definition: īnferius adj. neut. of inferior, lower, further down: Inferius terras (cremabis), too low, O.: inferius suis fraternos currere equos, O.—With quam, O.

infernus.definition: īnfernus adj. inferus, lower, under: sese infernis de partibus erigit Hydra: stagna, L.—Underground, of the lower regions, infernal: superi infernique di, L.: rex, Pluto, V.: gurges, O.: aspectus, revolting, Ta.

infero.definition: īn-ferō intulī, inlātus (ill-), īnferre, to bring in, introduce, bring to, carry in: nihil pati vini inferri, be imported, Cs.: peregrinos pecunia mores Intulit, introduced, Iu.: pedem, make an entrance: huc pedem, H.…

inferus.definition: īnferus adj. with comp. (see īnferior) and sup. (see īnfimus and īmus) cf. infra, below, beneath, underneath, lower: ut omnia supera, infera, videremus: mare, the Tuscan Sea.—As subst n.: navigatio infero, upon the Tu…

infervesco.definition: īn-fervēscō ferbuī, ere, inch. in-ferveo, to boil, stew, simmer: Hoc ubi inferbuit, H.

infeste.definition: īnfēstē adv. with comp. and sup. infestus, inimically, violently, outrageously: quae in nos fecerint, L.: infestius circumscindere, L.: infestissime contendere.

infesto.definition: īnfēstō —, —, āre infestus, to annoy, disturb, infest: latus dextrum, O.

infestus.definition: īnfēstus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of * infendo, made unsafe, disturbed, molested, infested, unquiet, unsafe: via excursionibus barbarorum: omnia serpentibus, S.: sua tuta omnia, infesta hostium, L.: vita: infestum …

inficio.definition: īnficiō fēcī, fectus, ere 1 in+facio, to stain, tinge, dye, color: (vestīs) quarum graminis ipsum Infecit natura pecus, i. e. whose wool has taken color from the pasture, Iu.: diem, darken, O.: ora pallor inficit, ove…

infidelis.definition: īn-fidēlis e, adj. with sup, not to be trusted, unfaithful, faithless: fides infideli data: qui ante erant per se infideles, Cs.: arbitrae, H.: infidelissimi (socii): Novis rebus Allobrox, in times of change, H.

infidelitas.definition: īnfidēlitās ātis, f infidelis, unfaithfulness, faithlessness, infidelity: infidelitatis suspicio, Cs.: quantae infidelitates in amicis.

infideliter.definition: īnfidēliter adv., faithlessly, perfidiously: nec aliquid senatui suadere.

infidus.definition: īn-fīdus adj., not to be trusted, unsafe, faithless, treacherous, false: amici: nihil stabile quod infidum est: genus Numidarum, S.: scurra, H.: pax, L.: gens ad occasiones, Ta.

infigo.definition: īn-fīgō fīxī, fīxus, ere, to fasten, implant, drive in, affix: ferreis hamis infixis, Cs.: portae infigitur hasta, V.: signum: infixum volnus, i. e. deep, V.: laevo infixa est lateri manus, was nailed to, V.: sagitta …

infimus.definition: īnfimus or īnfumus adj. sup. cf. inferus, lowest, last (cf. ī mus, but of the lowest of several objects, infimus is used): radices montis, Cs.: cum scripsissem haec infima: arā, lowest part: sub infimo colle, foot, Cs…

infindo.definition: īn-findō fidī, fissus, ere, to cut into, cleave: telluri sulcos, V.: sulcos (in sailing), V.

infinitas.definition: īnfīnitās ātis, f 2 in+finis, boundlessness, endlessness, infinity: in infinitatem omnem peregrinari (sc. animo): locorum: naturae.

infinite.definition: īnfīnītē adv. infinitus, without bounds, without end, infinitely: ne infinite feratur ut flumen oratio: quod faciendum est in perorando, without restraint.—Without exception, universally: res infinite posita.

infinitio.definition: īnfīnītiō ōnis, f infinitus, boundlessness, infinity: ipsa.

infinitus.definition: īn-fīnītus adj. with comp, not limited, infinite, endless, boundless, unlimited: altitudo: imperium: domini infinitā potestate, L.: sin cuipiam nimis infinitum videtur, too vast: quos erat infinitum nominare, an endle…

infirmatio.definition: īnfīrmātiō ōnis, f infirmo, a weakening, invalidating: Rerum iudicatarum: rationis, refutation.

infirme.definition: īnfīrmē adv. infirmus, faintly, slightly: animatus.

infirmitas.definition: īnfīrmitās ātis, f infirmus, want of strength, weakness, feebleness: valetudinis: corporis.—The weaker sex: patiendum huic infirmitati est, quodcumque, etc., L.—Fig., feebleness, infirmity: Quid habent infirmitatis nu…

infirmo.definition: īnfīrmō āvī, ātus, āre infirmus, to weaken, invalidate, disprove, refute, impair, annul: legiones, Ta.: res tam levī s: ad iudicem fidem testis: ceteras (leges), L.

infirmus.definition: īn-fīrmus adj. with comp. and sup, not strong, weak, feeble, infirm: vires: corpus annis, S.: classis: oves, H.: ex gravi morbo, ill: infirmi ad resistendum, Cs.—Fig., weak, superstitious, pusillanimous, inconstant, l…

infit.definition: īn-fit defect, begins: ita farier, V.—Begins to speak; his vocibus infit, V.: ita Tullus infit: Romani, etc., L.: ibi infit, se agere, etc., L.: causam scitantibus infit, O.

infitiae.definition: (īnfitiae, ārum) f 2 in+1 FA-, denial.— Only acc., in the phrase, infitias ire, to deny: quod nemo it infitias, N.: neque infitias eo, nos dedisse, etc., L.: ille infitias ibit, T.: infitias eunt mercedem se pactos, L.

infitialis.definition: īnfitiālis e, adj. infitiae, negative, consisting in denial: quaestio.

infitiatio.definition: īnfitiātiō ōnis, f infitior, a denial.

infitiator.definition: īnfitiātor ōris, m infitior, a denier, repudiator, shuffler: ille: lentus, a bad debtor.

infitior.definition: īnfitior ātus, ārī, dep. infitiae, not to confess, to contradict, deny, disown: non infitiando confiteri videbantur: cum id posset infitiari, repente confessus est: in quā me non infitior esse versatum. — Pass: Progen…

inflammatio.definition: īnflammātiō ōnis, f inflammo, a kindling, firing: inflammationem agris inferre.—Fig.: animorum.

inflammo.definition: īn-flammō āvī, ātus, āre, to set on fire, light up, kindle: taedas ignibus: urbem: classem: tecta, L.—Fig., to inflame, kindle, rouse, excite: contionibus invidiam senatūs: inflammari cupiditate honorum: animum amore,…

inflate.definition: (īnflātē) adv. 1 inflatus.—Only comp, haughtily, proudly, pompously: inflatius commemorare, Cs.: haec perscribebat, with exaggeration, Cs.

inflatio.definition: īnflātiō ōnis, f inflo, a puffing up, flatulence: habet inflationem (faba), produces flatulence.

inflatus1.definition: īnflātus adj. with comp. P. of inflo, swelled up, swollen, puffed up: serpens inflato collo: amnes, L.—Fig., puffed up, inflated, haughty, proud: animus: regis pollicitationibus, Cs.: promissis: iactatione, L.: his op…

inflatus2.definition: īnflātus ūs, m inflo, a blowing in, blast: (tibiae) si inflatum non recipiunt: primo inflatu tibicinis.—Fig., a breathing into, inspiration: divinus.

inflecto.definition: īn-flectō ēxī, exus, ere, to bend, bow, curve, turn aside: cum ferrum se inflexisset, Cs.: inflexum aratrum, V.: sinus ad urbem inflectitur, curves: suo squalore vestros oculos, turn aside.—Fig., to change, alter, inf…

infletus.definition: īn-flētus adj., unwept, unlamented: turba, V.

inflexio.definition: īnflexiō ōnis, f 1 in+FALC-, a bending: helicis: laterum fortis, vigorous attitude.

inflexus2.definition: īnflexus ūs, m 1 in+FALC-, a bending, curving: vicorum, Iu.

infligo.definition: īnflīgō īxī, īctus, ere 1 in + * fligo; 1 FLAG-, to dash upon, strike against: rei p. securim: cratera viro, O.: puppis inflicta vadis. V.—Fig.: cum ex eo (verbo) in ipsum aliquid infligitur, is hurled at.—To inflict:…

inflo.definition: īn-flō āvī, ātus, āre, to blow into, blow, inflate, swell: simul inflavit tibicen: paulo inflavit vehementius, i. e. wrote in a loftier style: calamos levīs, V.: (bucina) cecinit inflata receptūs, O.: pellem, Ph.: ill…

influo.definition: īn-fluō uxī, uxus, ere, to flow in, run in: ut influat in urbis sinum portus: locus qui in flumen influit, Cs.: mare, quo Rhenus influit, Cs.: huc Sagaris influit, O.—To stream in, throng in, invade: influentes in Ita…

infodio.definition: īn-fodiō fōdī, fossus, ere, to bury, inter: squalentī s conchas, V.: taleae in terram infodiebantur, Cs.: corpus procul ab eo loco, N.: infossus puer, H.

informatio.definition: īn-fōrmātiō ōnis, f informo, a representation, idea, conception: antecepta animo rei: dei.

informis.definition: īnfōrmis e, adj. 2 in+forma, without form, unformed, shapeless: alveus, L.: materia, Ta.— Unshapely, misshapen, deformed, distorted, hideous, horrible: monstrum, V.: hiemes, H.: letum, disfiguring, V.: aggeribus Terra…

informo.definition: īn-fōrmō āvī, ātus, āre, to shape, mould, fashion: clipeum, V.: His informatum manibus Fulmen erat, forged, V.—Fig., to constitute, organize: animus a naturā bene informatus.—To inform, instruct, educate: ad indicium …

infortunatus.definition: īn-fortūnātus adj. with comp, unfortunate, ill-starred: senex, T.: nihil me infortunatius.

infortunium.definition: īnfortūnium ī, n 2 in+fortuna, a misfortune, calamity: ferres infortunium, wouldst come badly off, T.: habiturus infortunium, L.— Plur: tua me laedent, H.

infra1.definition: īnfrā adv. for inferā, sc. parte, on the under side, below, underneath: infra nihil est nisi mortale: partes eae, quae sunt infra quam id quod devoratur: infra Quam solet esse, O.: exemplum infra scriptum est, S.: one…

infra2.definition: īnfrā praep. with acc. 1 infra, below, under, beneath: infra oppidum: infra caelum nox cadit, Ta.—Of time, later than: Homerus non infra superiorem Lycurgum fuit.—Of size, smaller than: magnitudine paulo infra elephan…

infractio.definition: īnfrāctiō ōnis, f 1 in+FRAC-, a breaking, weakening: animi, despondency.

infractus.definition: īnfrāctus adj. P. of infringo, broken, exhausted, weakened, subdued: infractos animos gerere, L.: oratio, L.: fama, injured, V.: Latini, broken, V.—Of speech: infracta et amputata loqui, disconnectedly.

infragilis.definition: īn-fragilis e, adj., strong, unwearied: vox, O.

infremo.definition: (īn-fremō) uī, —, ere, to make a noise, growl, bellow (only perf.): infremuitque ferox, V.: quotiens Lucilius Infremuit, raged, Iu.

infrenatus1.definition: īn-frēnātus adj., without a bridle: equites infrenati, on unbridled horses, L.

infrendo.definition: (īn-frendō, —, —, ere) to gnash.—Only P. praes.: dentibus infrendens gemitu, V.

infrenis.definition: īnfrēnis —, adj. 2 in+frenum, without a bridle, unbridled: equus, V.

infreno.definition: īn-frēnō —, ātus, āre, to put on a bridle, furnish with a bridle, bridle, harness, curb: non infrenatos equos habere, L.: currūs, to harness the horses to, V.—Fig., to curb, restrain: infrenatus conscientiā scelerum.

infrenus.definition: īnfrēnus adj. 2 in+frenum, unbridled: Numidae, riding without bridles, V.

infrequens.definition: īn-frequēns tis, adj. with comp. and sup, not crowded, in small numbers: copiae hoc infrequentiores imponuntur, in smaller numbers, Cs.: senatus, with no quorum: causa, thinly attended: infrequentissima urbis, the lea…

infrequentia.definition: īn-frequentia ae, f a small number, thinness, scantiness: nec agi quicquam per infrequentiam poterat senatūs, want of a quorum, L.: summā infrequentiā (sc. senatūs): locorum, loneliness, Ta.

infringo.definition: īnfringō frēgī, frāctus, ere in+frango, to break off, break, bruise: infractis omnibus hastis, L.: infracta tela, V.: violas Liliaque, O.: quibus (liminibus) latus, bruise on the threshold, H.: infractus remus (broken…

infrons.definition: īnfrōns ondis, adj. 2 in+frons, without foliage, destitute of trees: agri, O.

infructuosus.definition: īn-frūctuōsus adj., fruitless, unprofitable: militia, Ta.

infucatus.definition: īn-fūcātus adj., painted over, varnished: vitia, faults (of style) hidden by ornament.

infula.definition: īnfula ae, f 2 FAL-, a band, bandage: in infulis rem depingere.— A sacred fillet (a woolen band, white and red, worn upon the forehead by priests, victims, and suppliants, as a badge of consecration): sacerdotes Cerer…

infundo.definition: īn-fundō fūdī, fūsus, ere, to pour in, pour upon: in aliquod vas ea: oleum extis, V.: animas formatae terrae, i. e. people, O.— To pour out, administer, present: filio venenum: tibi poculum, H.: iumentis hordea, Iu.—T…

infusco.definition: īn-fuscō āvī, ātus, āre, to make dark, darken, obscure: vellera, V.—Fig., to obscure, sully, corrupt, stain: nec eos aliqua barbaries infuscaverat, corrupted their speech: sanie infuscatur harena, V.

ingemino.definition: in-geminō āvī, ātus, āre, to redouble, repeat, reiterate: dextrā ictūs, V.: vox adsensu nemorum ingeminata remugit, V.: Me miserum! ingeminat, O.—To redouble, multiply, be redoubled, increase: ingeminant austri, V.: c…

ingemisco.definition: ingemīscō —, —, ere, inch. ingemo, to utter a groan, heave a sigh, groan over: pueri non ingemiscunt: quantum ingemiscant patres nostri, si, etc., L.: in quo tu ingemiscis: ulli malo: (luce) repertā, V.: Dolabellam: i…

ingemo.definition: in-gemō uī, —, ere, to groan over, sigh at, mourn over, lament, bewail, mourn, groan, wail: tuum interitum, V.: in aliquā re: genitoris amore, V.: cuius morte ingemuit rex, Cu.: cuius (urbis) ruinis, L.: aratro, V.: l…

ingenero.definition: in-generō āvī, ātus, āre, to implant, engender, produce: amorem in eos qui, etc.: haec astro ingenerata, i. e. by desting: non ingenerantur hominibus mores.—To generate, create: animum esse ingeneratum a Deo.

ingeniose.definition: ingeniōsē adv. ingeniosus, acutely, wittily, ingeniously: nihil (excogitat): electas res conlocare, Iu.

ingeniosus.definition: ingeniōsus (ingenu-) adj. with comp. and sup. ingenium, full of intellect, superior in mind, able, intellectual, clever, ingenious: adulescens: quo quisque est ingeniosior: homo ingeniosissimus: in poenas, O.—Adapted,…

ingenitus.definition: ingenitus adj. P. of ingigno, innate, inborn.

ingenium.definition: ingenium ī, n 1 in+GEN-, innate quality, nature, temperament, constitution: locorum hominumque ingenia, L.: arvorum, V.: ferae bestiae, praecipitia ingenia sortitae, Cu.—Natural disposition, temper, character, bent, i…

ingens.definition: ingēns tis, adj. with comp. 2 in+GEN-, not natural, immoderate, vast, huge, prodigious, enormous, great, remarkable: agere gratias mihi Ingentī s, T.: magnitudo corporum, Cs.: praeda: pecunia, exorbitant: aes alienum,…

ingenue.definition: ingenuē adv. ingenuus, as becomes his birth, liberally, frankly: educatus: confiteri.

ingenuitas.definition: ingenuitās ātis, f ingenuus, free birth: ius ingenuitatis.— Fig., generosity, ingenuousness, frankness: prae se probitatem quandam et ingenuitatem ferre: praestare ingenuitatem.

ingenuus.definition: ingenuus adj. 1 in + GEN-, native, indigenous: tophus, Iu.—Natural: color, Pr.—Free-born, of free parents: mulieres: duobus ingenuis ortus, L.: parentes, H.—Subst: quid est turpius ingenuo, quam, etc.: ingenuam nactus…

ingero.definition: in-gerō (imper. inger, Ct.), gessī, gestus, ere, to throw in, pour in, heap upon: quicquid vinei oleique erat, oribus ingerebatur, Cu.: ingesta est insula membris, O.: alcui calices amariores, Ct.— To inflict, hurl, c…
