ingigno.definition: (in-gīgnō) genuī, genitus, ere, to implant, engender: cupiditatem homini: animantibus conservandi sui custodiam.

inglorius.definition: inglōrius adj. 2 in+gloria, without fame, unhonored, inglorious: qui sunt inglorii: vita: parmā albā, inconspicuous, V.: militiae, Ta.: remeabo inglorius, without trophies, V.: inglorium arbitrabatur (with infin.), Ta.

ingluvies.definition: ingluviēs —, acc. em, abl. ē, f GVOR-, the crop, maw: hic piscibus atram ingluviem explet, V.: parentis stringere ingluvie rem, gluttony, H.

ingrate.definition: ingrātē adv. ingratus, unpleasantly: Sunt quibus ingrate indulgentia servit, O.—Unthankfully, ungratefully: necessitudinis nomen repudiare.

ingratificus.definition: ingrātificus adj. ingratus + 2 FAC-, unthankful, ungrateful: Argivi.

ingratiis.definition: in-grātiīs (T., C.) or in-grātīs (C., N.), adv., without thanks, unwillingly, involuntarily, on compulsion: coacta ingratiis, T.: ingratiis ut dormiam, T.: nisi plane cogit ingratiis: dicent quae necesse erit, ingrati…

ingratus.definition: in-grātus adj. with comp. and sup, unpleasant, disagreeable, unacceptable: litterae: labor, S.: iocus, O.: oratio Gallis, Cs.: Veneri superbia, H.— Unthankful, ungrateful: in te: in deserendo: in referendā gratiā, Cs.…

ingravesco.definition: in-gravēscō —, —, ere, inch. ingravo, to grow burdensome, be wearied: corpora exercitationum defatigatione ingravescunt.—To increase, be aggravated, grow worse: morbus ingravescens: ingravescens aetas: in dies, become…

ingravo.definition: in-gravō āvī, ātus, āre, to weigh down, oppress, molest: annis ingravantibus, Ph.—To render worse, aggravate: ingravat haec Drances, V.: meos casūs, O.

ingredior.definition: ingredior essus, ī, dep. 1 in+gradior, to advance, go forward, march, proceed: si stas, ingredere; si ingrederis, curre: Ingredere, o ductor, V.: pedes per nives et glaciem ingredi coepit, Cu.: tardius: quācumque, O.:…

ingressio.definition: ingressiō ōnis, f 1 in+GRAD-, a going into, entering: fori, entrance.—Of speech, a beginning, exordium: in oratione moderata.

ingressus2.definition: ingressus ūs, m 1 in+GRAD-, an advancing, walking, gait: ingressus, cursus, accubitio: prohiberi ingressu, could not stir, Cs.: instabilis, L.— Fig.: ingressūs capere, begins, V.—A going in, entering: in forum: ingres…

ingruo.definition: ingruō uī, —, ere GAL-, to break in, come violently, assault in force, fall upon: fert Ingruere hostīs, V.: Italis, V.: si bellum ingrueret, V.: ferreus ingruit imber, V.: ingruere morbi in remiges coeperunt, L.: ab c…

inguen.definition: inguen inis, n ANG-, the groin: destillat ab inguine virus, V.: candida succincta inguina (Scylla), V.: ventrem atque inguina hausit, L.—A swelling, tumor.— The privy parts, H., O., Iu.

ingurgito.definition: ingurgitō āvī, ātus, āre 1 in + gurges, to gorge, stuff: se.—Fig., with se, to be absorbed in, addict oneself to: se in flagitia.

ingustatus.definition: in-gustātus adj., not tasted before: ilia rhombi, H.

inhabilis.definition: 'in-habilis e, adj., unmanageable, unwieldy: navis inhabilis prope magnitudinis, L.: multitudo ad consensum, L.: hostibus, awkward, Ta.'

inhaereo.definition: in-haereō haesī, haesus, ere, to stick fast, cling, cleave, adhere, inhere: quorum linguae inhaererent: inhaesuro similis (canis), as if about to fasten on her, O.: dextram amplexus inhaesit, V.: animi, qui corporibus…

inhaeresco.definition: inhaerēscō —, —, ere inch. inhaereo, to stick fast, cleave, adhere: in sordibus: eminere ubi ignis hostium inhaeresceret, Cs.— Fig.: poëtae inhaerescunt penitus in mentibus.

inhalo.definition: in-hālō āvī, —, āre, to breathe upon: nobis popinam, the smell of food that has been eaten.

inhibeo.definition: inhibeō uī, ītus, ēre 1 in+habeo, to hold in, hold back, keep back, restrain, curb, check: tela, V.: frenos, L.: cruorem, O.—To row backwards: cum inhiberent Rhodii, L.: remis, Cu.: retro navem, L.—To stop rowing: cum…

inhibitio.definition: inhibitiō ōnīs, f inhibeo, a reversing: remigum, rowing backwards.

inhio.definition: in-hiō āvī, ātus, āre, to stand open, gape, gaze, be amazed: inhians Cerberus, V.: attonitis inhians animis, V.: uberibus lupinis inhians: postīs, gape at, V.—To gaze eagerly, regard longingly: congestis undique sacci…

inhoneste.definition: inhonestē adv. inhonestus, dishonorably, disgracefully: parere divitias, T.: accusare.

inhonesto.definition: inhonestō —, —, āre inhonestus, to dishonor, disgrace: palmas adeptas, O.

inhonestus.definition: in-honestus adj. with sup, dishonorable, disgraceful, shameful: ignotā matre, H.: vita, S.: mors, L.: volnus, V.: lubido, S.: homo inhonestissimus.— Unseemly, repulsive: meretrices, T.

inhonoratus.definition: in-honōrātus adj. with comp. and sup, unhonored, disregarded: vita: inhonoratior triumphus, L.: dea, O.—Without reward, unrewarded: regem inhonoratum dimittere, L.: gentium inhonoratissimi post victoriam, L.: nos, O.

inhonorus.definition: in-honōrus adj., unsightly: signa, defaced, Ta.

inhorreo.definition: in-horreō —, —, ēre, to stand erect, bristle: haud secus quam vallo saepta inhorreret acies, L.

inhorresco.definition: in-horrēscō uī, —, ere, inch, to stand erect, bristle up, rise in points, roughen, ruffle: inhorrescit mare: inhorruit unda tenebris, V.: mobilibus vepris inhorruit Ad ventos foliis, H.: aper inhorruit armos, bristled…

inhospitalis.definition: in-hospitālis e, adj., inhospitable: Caucasus, H.

inhospitus.definition: 'in-hospitus adj., inhospitable: tecta, O.: saxa, V.: tesqua, H.'

inhumane.definition: inhūmānē adv. with comp. inhumanus, cruelly, inhumanly: cruciat adulescentulum, T.: inhumanius dicere.

inhumanitas.definition: inhūmānitās ātis, f inhumanus, inhuman conduct, barbarity: immoderata.—Incivility, rudeness, brutality: quod ego non superbiā neque inhumanitate faciebam: omni aetati molesta.— Unkindness, disobligingness: nulla inhum…

inhumaniter.definition: inhūmāniter adv. inhumanus, uncivilly, discourteously: fecisse: respondit.

inhumanus.definition: in-hūmānus adj. with comp. and sup, rude, savage, barbarous, brutal, inhuman: quis tam inhumanus, qui, etc.: vox: scelus, L.: testamentum, unjust.—Unpolished, unsocial, uncivil, without culture, unmannerly, ill-bred, …

inhumatus.definition: in-humātus unburied: nec inhumati nec deserti: Coniunx, V.

inibi.definition: in-ibi adv., therein, in that place, there: superbia nata inibi esse videtur (i. e. Capuae).— Fig.: aut inibi esse, aut iam esse confectum, just at hand.

inicio.definition: iniciō (iniiciō), iēcī, iectus, ere 1 in+iacio, to throw in, put in, hurl upon, put on, cast on, set into: domus ardebat ignibus iniectis: eo militibus iniectis (i. e. in navīs), Cs.: dextram accenso foculo, L.: iniec…

iniectus2.definition: (iniectus) ūs, m inicio, a casting on, throwing over.—Only abl: multae vestis, Ta.

inimice.definition: inimīcē adv. with comp. and sup. inimicus, as an enemy, inimically: tecum agere: insectari: inimicius consulere, L.: inimicissime contendere.

inimicitia.definition: inimīcitia ae, f inimicus, enmity, hostility: inimicitia (est) ira ulciscendi, etc.—Usu. plur: inimicitias capere in familiam, T.: erant ei veteres inimicitiae cum Rosciis: inimicitias mihi denuntiare: inimicitias rei…

inimico.definition: inimīcō —, —, āre inimicus, to make hostile, set at variance: miseras urbīs, H.

inimicus.definition: inimīcus adj. with comp. and sup. 2 in+amicus, unfriendly, hostile, inimical: capere inimicos homines, incur the enmity of, T.: inimicior eram huic quam Caesari: animo inimico venisse: Pompeio, S.: sibi omnīs esse ini…

inique.definition: inīquē adv. with comp. and sup. iniquus, unequally: Quam inique comparatum est, T.: iniquius Certatio comparata, more unequally matched, T.: iniquissime comparatum est.—Fig., unfairly, unjustly: damnati: occidere, L.:…

iniquitas.definition: inīquitās ātis, f iniquus, inequality, unevenness: loci, Cs.: in talibus iniquitatibus locorum, L.—Fig., unfavorableness, difficulty, hardness: loci, L.: rerum, Cs.: temporum.—Unfairness, injustice, unreasonableness: …

iniquus.definition: inīquus adj. with comp. and sup. 2 in+ aequus, uneven, slanting, steep: puppis dorso dum pendet iniquo, V.: subire iniquo ascensu, L.: locus iniquor, Cs.: mons, O.—Unequal, ill-matched: pugna, V.—Excessive: onus, L.: …

initio.definition: initiō āvī, ātus, āre initium, to begin, initiate, consecrate, admit: Ubi initiabunt (puerum), T.: initiari eo ritu Cereri: initiari Bacchis, L.—Fig.: quae (sica) abs te initiata sacris.

initium.definition: initium ī, n 1 in + 1 I-, a going in, entrance: Remorum, i. e. of the country, Cs.—Fig., a beginning, commencement: Narrationis, T.: annorum, Cs.: bonis initiis orsus tribunatus, tristīs exitus habuit consulatus: bell…

initus2.definition: initus ūs, m 1 in+1 I-, an entrance, O.

iniucunde.definition: (iniūcundē) adv. iniucundus, unpleasantly. —Only comp: res iniucundius actae.

iniucunditas.definition: iniūcunditās ātis, f iniucundus, unpleasantness: ne quid habeat iniucunditatis oratio.

iniucundus.definition: in-iūcundus adj., unpleasant, disagreeable: minime nobis labor: adversus malos, harsh, Ta.

iniungo.definition: in-iungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere, to join, fasten, attach: tignos in asseres, L.: vineas moenibus.— Fig., to inflict, impose, enjoin, occasion, bring upon: civitatibus servitutem, Cs.: privatis onus, L.: iniuriam a nobis re…

iniuratus.definition: in-iūrātus adj., unsworn, not under oath: cum dicit iniuratus: iurati iniuratique fugiunt, L.

iniuria.definition: iniūria ae, f iniurius, an injustice, wrong, outrage, injury, insult: (filius) carens patriā ob meas iniurias, harsh treatment, T.: paterna, T.: iniuriam sibi imponere: privatas iniurias ultus est, Cs.: in populum R.,…

iniuriose.definition: iniūriōsē adv. with comp. iniuriosus, unjustly, unlawfully: in alqo decernere: tractati.

iniuriosus.definition: iniūriōsus adj. iniuria, unjust, wrongful, harmful: in proximos: ab invito emere iniuriosum esse: pes, H.

iniurius.definition: iniūrius adj. 2 in+ius, unlawful, injurious, wrongful, unjust: sibi esse iniurius videri, T.: Id possum ferre quamquam iniuriumst, T.: quia sit iniurium: indictā causā damnari absentem iniurium esse, L.

iniussus1.definition: in-iūssus adj., unbidden, voluntary, of one's own accord: cantare Iniussi numquam desistant, H.: iniussae veniunt ad mulctra capellae, H.: iniussa virescunt Gramina, spontaneous, V.—Plur n. as subst: Non iniussa cano,…

iniussus2.definition: (in-iūssus, ūs) m without command.—Only abl: iniussu suo et civitatis, Cs.: iniussu praetoris: signa referunt, without orders, L.

iniuste.definition: iniūstē adv. with sup. iniustus, without right, unjustly: facere: totum ducit poema, H.: iniustissime, S.

iniustitia.definition: iniūstitia ae, f iniustus, injustice, unfairness: iniustitiae duo genera sunt.—Severity, harshness: Eum ego hinc eieci iniustitiā meā , T.

iniustus.definition: in-iūstus adj. with comp. and sup, unreasonable, unsuitable, oppressive, excessive, improper, severe, burdensome: iusta iniusta omnia obsequi, humor you in everything, T.: onus: fascis, V.: supplicia, S.: faenus, L.—U…

inlabefactus.definition: 'in-labefactus (ill-) adj., unbroken, uninterrupted: adfinia vincula, O.: concordia, O.'

inlabor.definition: in-lābor (ill-) lapsus, ī, dep., to flow in, glide in, fall, sink: Si fractus inlabatur orbis, fall to ruins, H.: quo (in stomachum) primo inlabuntur ea, etc.: mediae urbi, V.—Fig., to flow in, penetrate: ad eos (sens…

inlaboro.definition: in-labōrō (ill-) —, —, āre, to work upon, work at: domibus (i. e. aedificandis), Ta.

inlacessitus.definition: in-lacessītus (ill-) adj., unprovoked, unattacked: pacem inlacessiti nutrierunt, Ta.: Britanniae pars, undisturbed, Ta.

inlacrimabilis.definition: in-lacrimābilis (ill-) e, adj., unwept, unlamented: omnes inlacrimabiles Urgentur Nocte, H. —Not moved by tears, pitiless: Pluto, H.

inlacrimo.definition: inlacrimō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 in+lacrima, dep., to weep over, sorrow for, bewail, lament: qui dicitur inlacrimans dixisse: Sic ait inlacrimans, V.: gaudio, L.: inlacrima patris pestibus: casu, N.: maestum inlacrim…

inlacrimor.definition: inlacrimor ātus, ārī, dep. 1 in+lacrima, to weep over, lament: inlacrimare, H.: cuius morti.

inlaesus.definition: 'in-laesus (ill-) adj., unhurt, unharmed, unmutilated: inlaeso corpore, O.: partes, O.'

inlaetabilis.definition: in-laetābilis (ill-) e, adj., cheerless, joyless, gloomy, sad: ora, V.: murmur, V.

inlaqueo.definition: in-laqueō (ill-) —, ātus, āre 1 in+laqueus, to ensnare, entrap, entangle: munera navium inlaqueant duces, H.: inlaqueatus legum periculis.

inlaudatus.definition: in-laudātus (ill-) adj., unpraised, infamous: Busiris, V.

inlecebra.definition: 'inlecebra (ill-) ae, f 1 in+1 LAC-, an enticement, inducement, attraction, charm, allurement, bait, lure: ad quam inlecebram cum commoveretur nemo, etc., L.: suis te oportet inlecebris virtus trahat: inlecebris erat …

inlepide.definition: inlepidē (ill-) adv. inlepidus, impolitely, rudely, inelegantly: (poema) Compositum, H.

inlepidus.definition: 'in-lepidus (ill-) adj., unmannerly, rude, disagreeable: parens, Caecil. ap. C.: deliciae, Ct.'

inlibatus.definition: in-lībātus (ill-) adj., undiminished, unimpaired: divitiae: vires, L.: imperium, L.

inliberalis.definition: in-līberālis (ill-) e, adj., ignoble, ungenerous, vulgar, sordid, mean, disobliging: quaestūs: facinus, T.: iocandi genus: Servos, T.: in me, disobliging.—Niggardly, petty: adiectio, L.

inliberalitas.definition: inlīberālitās (ill-) ātis, f inliberalis, meanness, stinginess: inliberalitatis suspicio.

inliberaliter.definition: inlīberāliter (ill-) adv. inliberalis, ignobly, ungenerously, meanly: factum a vobis, T.: aestimare, i. e. stingily.

inlicio.definition: inliciō (ill-) lexī, lectus, ere (inlēxe for inlēxisse, Att. ap. C.) 1 in+lacio, to allure, entice, attract, seduce, inveigle, decoy: coniugem in stuprum: Imperitos rerum in fraudem, T.: inlecti <*>d proditionem, S.: …

inlicitator.definition: inlicitātor (ill-) ōris, m * inlicitor, a shambidder, bidder-in, mock-purchaser: non inlicitatorem apponet: ponere.

inlicitus.definition: 'in-licitus (ill-) adj., not allowed, unlawful, illicit: amor, Ta.: exactiones, Ta.'

inlido.definition: inlīdō (ill-) sī, sus, ere 1 in+laedo, to dash against, push against: caestūs effracto in ossa cerebro, V.: ad volnus manūs: pila vadis inlisa, V.: repagula ossibus, O.: dentem fragili (corpori), H.—To crush: serpens …

inligo.definition: in-ligō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bind on, tie on, fasten, attach: tauris iuga, H.: inligata tigna tenere, Cs.: manibus post tergum inligatis, L.: emblemata in poculis: litterae in iaculo inligatae, Cs.: lunae motūs i…

inlimis.definition: inlīmis (ill-) e, adj. 2 in+limus, without mud: fons, i. e. clear, O.

inlino.definition: in-linō (ill-) lēvī, litus, ere, to smear over, spread upon, lay on: oculis collyria, H.: nivīs agris, spreads, H.: alqd chartis, has written, H.— To besmear, bedaub, anoint: malleolos stuppae pice, L.: texta Nesseo v…

inlitteratus.definition: inlitterātus (ill-) adj., unlettered, unlearned, without culture, inelegant: multi: in sermone multa: nervi, H.

inlotus.definition: in-lōtus (ill-), or in-lautus adj., unwashed, unclean, dirty: toralia, H.—Not washed away: sudor, V.

inlucesco.definition: in-lūcēscō (ill-) lūxī, —, ere, inch, to grow light, begin to shine, break, dawn: Inlucescet aliquando ille dies, cum, etc.: cum tertio die sol inluxisset: alios Inluxisse dies, V.—Perf impers., it was light, day had …

inludo.definition: in-lūdō (ill-) sī (inlūsseris, C.), sus, ere, to play at, sport with: haec Inludo chartis, sportively throw on paper, H.: Inlusae auro vestes, gayly inwrought, V. (al. inclusae).—To make sport, make game of, mock, jee…

inlumino.definition: in-lūminō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre, to light up, make light, illuminate: luna inluminata a sole.— Fig., in rhet., to set off, illustrate: tamquam stellis orationem: illuminata sapientia.

inlusio.definition: inlūsiō (ill-) ōnis, f LVD-, a mocking, jeering.

inlustre.definition: (inlūstrē) adv. inlustris, clearly, manifestly. —Only comp: inlustrius (vidi me amari).

inlustris.definition: inlūstris (ill-) e, adj. with comp. LVC-, lighted, bright, light, lustrous, brilliant: domicilia: caput, O.: solis candor inlustrior est quam ullius ignis.—Fig., clear, plain, distinct, evident, manifest: ad cognoscen…

inlustro.definition: in-lūstrō (ill-) āvī, ātus, āre, to light up, make light, illuminate: quā sol Inlustrat oras, H.—Fig., to make clear, clear up, elucidate, illustrate, disclose, explain: ut ea consilia inlustrarentur: si modo id patef…

inluvies.definition: inluviēs (ill-) —, abl. ē, f 1 in+3 LV-, an overflow, inundation: gravesque currūs inluvie haerebant, in the mud, Cu.—A wash, offscouring, dirt, filth, uncleanness: inmunda inluvie, T.: pectus inluvie scabrum: inluvie…

innabilis.definition: innābilis e, adj. 2 in+NA-, in which one cannot swim: unda, O.

innascor.definition: in-nāscor nātus, ī, dep., to be born in, grow upon, spring up in: filix innascitur agris, H.: innata rupibus altis Robora, O.—Fig., to arise in, originate in, be produced in: cupiditas belli ge-rendi innata est, Cs.: …

innato.definition: in-natō āvī, ātus, are, to swim in, float upon: lactuca innatat acri stomacho, H.: undam innatat alnus, swims the stream, V.: innatat unda freto, flows over, O.—To swim into: in concham.

innatus.definition: innātus adj. P. of innascor, native, inborn, innate, inherent, natural: cupiditas scientiae: amor, V.: murex, native, O.: vecordia quoiquam, T.: ingeniis semina virtutum: alacritas naturaliter omnibus, Cs.: in nobis c…

innavigabilis.definition: in-nāvigābilis e, adj., not navigable: Tiberis, L.

innecto.definition: in-nectō nēxuī, nexus, ere, to twist, entangle, bind up, weave in, gather together, weave: comas, V.: ramum olivae (in crinīs), V.— To join, bind, attach, connect, fasten to, weave about: palmas armis, V.: tempora ser…

innitor.definition: in-nītor nīxus (-nīsus, Ta.), ī, dep., to lean upon, support oneself by: innititur hastae, O.: moli, O.: scutis innixi, Cs.: hastā innixus, L.

inno.definition: in-nō āvī, ātus, āre, to swim in, float upon: Partim submersae, partim innantes beluae: innabant pariter fluctūsque secabant, V.: aquae, L.: rapacīs fluvios, V.: fluvium, V.—To flow against, wash: innantem Maricae lit…

innocens.definition: in-nocēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup, harmless, inoffensive, innoxious: epistula: innocentis pocula Lesbii, H.—Blameless, guiltless, innocent: innocens si accusatus sit: tu innocentior quam Metellus?: innocentissi…

innocenter.definition: 'innocenter adv. with comp. innocens, blamelessly, innocently: opes paratae, Ta.: innocentius agere, Ta.'

innocentia.definition: in-nocentia ae, f innocens, blamelessness, innocence: eius innocentiam ostendere: solā innocentiā vivere, i. e. with no other support, L.— Uprightness, integrity, disinterestedness: quantā innocentiā debent esse imper…

innocuus.definition: in-nocuus adj., harmless, innocuous: herba, O.: litus, safe, V.: iter, undisputed, Ta.—Unharmed, uninjured: sedere carinae Omnes inno-cuae, V.— Inoffensive, innocent: viximus innocuae, O.: agere causas innocuas, defen…

innotesco.definition: in-nōtēscō tuī, —, ere, inch, to become known, be made conspicuous: quod ubi innotuit, L.: fraude, Ph.: nostris innotuit illa libellis, O.

innovo.definition: (in-novō) āvī, —, āre, to renew, restore: te ad tuam intemperantiam, i. e. return.

innoxius.definition: in-noxius adj., harmless, innoxious: anguis, V.—Not guilty, blameless, innocent: nominat multos innoxios, S.: illum innoxium plecti, N.: verba, V.: tactu flamma, V.: criminis innoxia, L.: initi consili in caput regis …

innubo.definition: in-nūbō nūpsī, nūptus, ere, to marry into: ea, quo innupsisset (the rank), into which she had married, L.: thalamis nostris, i. e. take my place as wife, O.

innubus.definition: 'innubus adj. NEB-, unmarried, single, virgin: vivere, O.: laurus (into which Daphne was changed), O.'

innumerabilis.definition: in-numerābilis e, adj., countless, innumerable, immeasurable, immense: copiae: pondus auri: frumenti numerus: annorum series, H.

innumerabilitas.definition: innumerābilitās ātis, f innumerabilis, countlessness, infinitude: mundorum: atomorum.

innumerus.definition: 'in-numerus adj., countless, innumerable, numberless: gentes, V.: pyrae, V.: sagittae, O.'

innuo.definition: innuō uī, —, ere 2 NV-, to nod, give a sign, intimate, hint: Ne mora sit, si innuerim, T.: ubi innuerint, L.: coram licet innuat, Iu.: mi, T.

innuptus.definition: in-nūptus adj., unmarried, unwedded, single: puellae, V.: Minerva, virgin, V.—As subst f., a virgin, V., Ct., Pr.—Poet.: innuptae nuptiae, i. e. unhappy.

innutritus.definition: in-nūtrītus P., nourished in, educated to: Caesar pessimis, in all vices, Ta.

inoblitus.definition: in-oblītus adj., not forgetful, mindful, O.

inobservabilis.definition: in-observābilis e, adj., unavoidable, undiscoverable: error, Ct.

inobservatus.definition: in-observātus adj., unobserved, unperceived: ille in herbis, O.: sidera, O.

inoffensus.definition: in-offēnsus adj., unobstructed, unhindered, uninterrupted: mare, V.: vita, placid, O.

inofficiosus.definition: in-officiōsus adj., undutiful: testamentum, i. e. violating natural affection.—Disobliging: in hos.

inolesco.definition: in-olēscō —, —, ere, to grow, grow upon: germen udo inolescere libro, V.—Fig., to sink in, become inveterate: Multa inolescere, V.

inopia.definition: inopia ae, f inops, want, lack, scarcity: summa omnium rerum, Cs.: loci, L.: argumentorum.—Want, need, indigence, poverty, scarcity, famine: Inopiā Coacta, T.: propter inopiam in egestate esse: amicitia ex inopiā nata…

inopinans.definition: in-opīnāns antis, adj., not expecting, taken by surprise: inopinantes nostri re novā perturbantur, Cs.: inopinante Curione, Cs.: rex in potestatem inopinanti (ei) venerat, N.: suis inopinantibus, L.

inopinato.definition: inopīnātō adv. inopinatus, unexpectedly: in castra inrumpere, L.

inopinatus.definition: in-opīnātus adj., not expected, unexpected, surprising: tibi haec inopinata: neque inopinatum mihi sit, L.—As subst n.: nihil inopinati accidit: ex inopinato, unexpectedly.

inopinus.definition: inopīnus adj. 2 AP-, unexpected: quies, V.: fors, V.: visus, O.

inops.definition: inops opis, adj. 2 in+ops, without resources, helpless, weak: inopes relicti a duce: nihil iuris humani relinquitur inopi, L.: solare inopem, V.: ab amicis: laudis conscendere carmen, unskilled, Pr.—Without possession…

inoratus.definition: in-ōrātus adj., not pleaded: re inoratā reverterunt, without presenting their case.

inordinatus.definition: in-ōrdinātus adj., not arranged, disordered, irregular: milites, L.: inordinati in proelium ruunt, L.—As subst n.: idque ex inordinato in ordinem adduxit, disorder.

inornatus.definition: in-ōrnātus adj., unadorned, without ornament: mulieres: capilli, O.: nomina et verba, plain, H.: Non meis Chartis inornatus, uncelebrated, H.

inquam.definition: inquam defect. (only praes: inquam, inquis, inquit, inquimus, inquiunt; imperf. inquiēbat; perf. inquiī, inquīstī; fut. inquiēs, inquiet; imper. inque), to say (after one or more words of a quotation): Sy. eccum me in…

inquies.definition: in-quiēs ētis, adj., restless, unquiet: Germanus, Ta.: animo, Ta.

inquieto.definition: inquiētō —, —, āre inquietus, to disturb: victoriam, Ta.

inquietus.definition: in-quiētus adj., restless, unquiet, disturbed: animus, L.: nox, L.: praecordia, H.

inquilinus.definition: inquilīnus adj. for * incolīnus, incola, of foreign birth: civis urbis Romae, S.—As subst, a sojourner, lodger, immigrant: te inquilino.

inquinate.definition: inquinātē adv. inquinatus, filthily, impurely: loqui.

inquinatus.definition: inquinātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of inquino, foul, befouled, polluted: aqua cadaveribus.—Fig., defiled, contaminated, impure, filthy, base: versus: nihil hoc homine inquinatius: ratio inquinatissima: quis in vol…

inquino.definition: inquinō āvī, ātus, āre, to befoul, stain, pollute, defile: merdis caput inquiner albis Corvorum, H.: inquinet arma situs, O.— Fig., to pollute, defile, corrupt, contaminate, debase: amicitiam nomine criminoso: splendo…

inquiro.definition: inquīrō sīvī (-sīsse, -sīssent, L.), sī tus, ere <*> in + quaero, to seek after, search for: corpus funeris causā inquisitum, L.—To search into, examine, investigate, scrutinize: honestas, quam natura maxime inquirit:…

inquisitio.definition: inquīsītiō ōnis, f QVAES-, a seeking, searching, examination, investigation: veri: adempto per inquisitiones loquendi commercio, espionage, Ta. —In law, an investigation, legal inquisition: accusatoris: annua, Ta.

inquisitor.definition: inquīsītor ōris, m inquiro, a searcher, an inspector, examiner: algae, Iu.—In law, an investigator, collector of evidence: Achaicus.

inraucesco.definition: inraucēscō (irr-) rausī, —, ere, inch. 1 in+ raucus, to become hoarse: paulum.

inreligiose.definition: inreligiōsē (irr-) adv. inreligiosus, impiously: discere, Ta.

inreligiosus.definition: in-religiōsus (irr-) adj., irreligious, impious: irreligiosum ratus ire, etc., L.

inremeabilis.definition: in-remeābilis (irr-) e, adj., not to be retraced, from which there is no return: error, V.: unda, i. e. the Styx, V.

inreparabilis.definition: in-reparābilis (irr-) adj., irreparable, irretrievable: tempus, V.

inrepo.definition: in-rēpō (irr-) rēpsī, —, ere, to creep in, slip in, be stealthily inserted, steal in: eloquentia inrepit in sensūs: in tabulas municipiorum: animos, Ta.

inreprehensus.definition: in-reprehēnsus (irr-) adj., blameless, without blame: probitas, O.: responsa, true, O.

inrequietus.definition: in-requiētus (irr-) adj., unquiet, restless, without repose: Enipeus, O.: Charybdis, O.—Disquieting, causing unrest: sors mea, O.: bella, O.

inresolutus.definition: in-resolūtus (irr-) adj., not loosened: vincula, O.

inretio.definition: inrētiō (irr-) īvī, ītus, īre 1 in+rete, to catch in a net, ensnare, entangle: beluam inretitam tenere.—Fig., to entrap, catch, entangle, ensnare, involve: tacentem te: alquem corruptelarum inlecebris: disputationum l…

inretortus.definition: 'in-retortus (irr-) adj., not turned back: oculo inretorto, without looking back, H.'

inreverentia.definition: 'in-reverentia (irr-) ae, f irreverence, disrespect: iuventutis, Ta.: adversus fas nefasque, Ta.'

inrevocabilis.definition: in-revocābilis (irr-) e, adj. with comp, not to be recalled, irrevocable, unalterable: in casum inrevocabilem se dare, L.: semel emissum volat inrevocabile verbum, H.: quo obscurior eo inrevocabilior, implacable, Ta.

inrevocatus.definition: in-revocātus (irr-) adj., not called back, without an encore, H.

inrideo.definition: in-rīdeō (irr-) rīsī, rīsus, ēre, to laugh at, joke, jeer, mock, ridicule: in re tantā, T.: ex muro, Cs.: mihi: inridentes responderunt, N.: periocum deos: vatem, V.: inrideor, T.: procos inrisa experiar, V.: quae inr…

inrigatio.definition: inrigātiō (irr-) ōnis, f inrigo, a watering, irrigation: agrorum.

inrigo.definition: in-rigō (irr-) āvī, ātus, āre, to water, irrigate, flood: Aegyptum Nilus inrigat: Circus Tiberi superfuso inrigatus, overflowed, L.: fontibus hortulos: inrigat culta auro, V.: inrigatus venas nectare, Ph.— To pour out…

inriguus.definition: in-riguus (irr-) adj., watering, supplying water, living: fons, V.: aqua, O.—Supplied with water, well-watered: hortus, H.: mero corpus, soaked, H.

inrisio.definition: inrīsiō (irr-) ōnis, f RID-, a deriding, mocking, mockery: civitas subiecta inrisioni tuae, scoffs: omnium.

inrisor.definition: inrīsor (irr-) ōris, m RID-, a derider, mocker, scoffer: orationis, C., Pr.

inrisus2.definition: inrīsus (irr-) ūs, m RID-, a scoffing, mocking, mockery, derision: inrisui fore, be a laughing-stock, Cs., Ta.: linguam ab inrisu exserens, out of mockery, L.

inritabilis.definition: inrītābilis (irr-) e, adj. inrito, excitable, irritable: animi: genus vatum, H.

inritamen.definition: inrītāmen (irr-) inis, n inrito, an incitement, incentive, provocation: opes, animi inritamen avari, O.: sua (tauri) inritamina Poeniceae vestes, O.

inritamentum.definition: inrītāmentum (irr-) ī, n inrito, an incitement, incentive, provocation, inducement, stimulus: inritamentis iras militum acuere, L.: gulae, S.: pacis, Ta.: opes, inritamenta malorum, O.: posita veno inritamenta luxui, …

inritatio.definition: inrītātiō (irr-) ōnis, f inrito, an incitement, stimulus: conviviorum, Ta.—Wrath, anger, irritation: animorum, L.

inrito.definition: inrītō (irr-) āvī, ātus, āre, to incite, excite, stimulate, instigate, provoke, exasperate, irritate: magis inritatus, T.: vi virum: Terra, irā inritata deorum, V.: tribunos ad certamen, L.: pectus inaniter, H.: cum f…

inritus.definition: inritus (irr-) adj. 2 in+ratus, undecided, unsettled, invalid, void, of no effect: quod modo erat ratum, inritum est, T.: testamentum: quaeque augur dira defixerit, inrita infectaque sunto.— Vain, useless, without eff…

inrogatio.definition: inrogātiō (irr-) ōnis, f inrogo, an imposing, adjudicating: multae.

inrogo.definition: in-rogō (irr-) āvī (inrogassit for inrogaverit, C.), ā tus, āre.—In law, to propose in opposition: privilegium: leges privatis hominibus.—To impose, appoint, ordain, inflict: multam: centum milium multa inrogata erat,…

inroro.definition: in-rōrō (irr-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bedew: terras, V.—To moisten, besprinkle, wet: extremo inrorat Aquarius anno, brings rain, V.: caput, O.: crinem aquis, O.: lacrimae misero de corpore Inrorant foliis, O.— To sprinkle…

inrumatio.definition: inrumātiō (irr-) ōnis, f beastly obscenity, Ct.

inrumo.definition: inrumō (irr-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 in+ruma (breast), to give suck, abuse obscenely, Ct.

inrumpo.definition: in-rumpō (irr-) rūpī, ruptus, ere, to break in, press in, force a way in, burst into, rush at, fall upon: inrumpere conari, Cs.: dixit et inrupit, O.: hostes pluribus agminibus inrupturi, Ta.: quocunque, O.: in castra…

inruo.definition: in-ruō (irr-) ruī, —, ere, to rush in, invade, press into, make an attack: quam mox inruimus? T.: ferro, V.: in aedīs, T.: vi in tectum: ne ille huc prorsus se inruat, T.—Fig., to force a way in, rush into, enter eage…

inruptio.definition: inruptiō (irr-) ōnis, f RVP-, a breaking in, invasion, incursion: armatorum in domum: etiamsi inruptio facta nulla sit.

insalubris.definition: īn-salūbris e, adj., unwholesome: cibi, Cu.: fluvius potui, Cu.

insalutatus.definition: īn-salūtātus adj., ungreeted, unsaluted (in tmesis): Inque salutatam linquo, V.

insanabilis.definition: īn-sānābilis e, adj. with comp, not to be healed, incurable: morbus.—Fig., irretrievable, without remedy, hopeless: contumeliae: nihil insanabilius, L.: caput tribus Anticyris, H.: scribendi cacoethes, Iu.

insane.definition: īnsānē adv. with comp. insanus, madly, insanely: in silvam non ligna feras insanius, H.

insania.definition: īnsānia ae, f insanus, unsoundness of mind, madness, frenzy, folly, senselessness: haec ad insaniam concupiverat, madly: adigis me ad insaniam, T.: quae tanta insania, cives? V.: summa, H.: nudus agas, minus est insan…

insaniens.definition: īnsāniēns ntis, adj. P. of insanio, foolish, unreasonable: sapientia, the foolishness of wisdom, H.

insanio.definition: īnsāniō (imperf: īnsānībat, T.), īvī , ītus, īre insanus, to be of unsound mind, be senseless, be without reason, be mad, rave: homo insanibat, T.: insanire omnibus videri: ex iniuriā insaniens exercitus, L.: cum rati…

insanitas.definition: īnsānitās ātis, f insanus, unsoundness, disease: mentis: animi.

insanus.definition: īn-sānus adj. with comp. and sup, of unsound mind, mad, insane: quod idem contigit insanis: maritus, Iu.—Violent, absurd, raging, foolish, frantic: homines ex stultis insanos facere, T.: homo insanissimus: uter est in…

insatiabilis.definition: īn-satiābilis e, adj. with comp, not to be satisfied, insatiable: avaritia, S.: crudelitas: humanus animus, L.: acquirendi votum, Iu.—Unsating, not cloying: varietas: insatiabilior species.

inscendo.definition: īnscendō —, —, ere 1 in+scando, to climb up, mount, ascend: in rogum.

insciens.definition: īn-sciēns entis, adj., unknowing, without knowledge, unaware: Insciens feci, T.: inscientibus ipsis, Cs.: utrum inscientem . . . fecisse, an scientem?: abi sis, insciens, simpleton, T.

inscienter.definition: īnscienter adv. insciens, ignorantly, inadvertently: facere: tuba inflata, L.

inscientia.definition: īn-scientia ae, f want of knowledge, ignorance, inexperience: implicata: volgi, Cs.: ducum, L.: locorum, Cs.: belli, N.: philosophiae.

inscite.definition: īnscītē adv. inscitus, unskilfully, clumsily, awkwardly: comparari: facta navis, L.: turpem putat lituram, H.

inscitia.definition: īnscītia ae, f inscitus, ignorance, inexperience, unskilfulness, awkwardness: vos non facere inscitiast, T.: id inscitia est: inscitiā exercitum perducere, etc., L.: temporis: veri, H.: aedificandi, Ta.: inscitia, qui…

inscitus.definition: īn-scītus adj. with comp, ignorant, foolish, blundering: Inscitum offerre iniuriam iniquomst, T.: quid est inscitius quam, etc.

inscius.definition: īn-scius adj. 2 SAC-, not knowing, ignorant: quem vos inscii ad mortem misistis, ignorantly: inscios inopinantīsque Menapios oppresserunt, Cs.: stupet inscius pastor, V.: omnium rerum: laborum, H.: esse utilitatem in …

inscribo.definition: in-scrībō īpsī, īptus, ere, to write upon, inscribe: in basi tropaeorum inscribi: sit inscriptum in fronte quid de re p. sentiat: si quae essent inscriptae litterae: in illis libellis: eum sotera inscriptum esse vidi,…

inscriptio.definition: inscrīptiō ōnis, f SCARP-, an inscribing: nominis.— An inscription, legend, title: statua cum inscriptione: plenior.

insculpo.definition: īn-sculpō (inscalp-) psī, ptus, ere, to cut in, carve upon, engrave: titulus Graecis litteris insculptus, L.: summam patrimoni saxo, H.: Cornua Postibus, O.: columnā aeneā insculptum, L. —Fig., to engrave, imprint: na…

inseco.definition: īn-secō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut into, cut up: gurgulionibus insectis: cutem, L.: insecti pectine dentes, notched, O.

insectatio.definition: īnsectātiō ōnis, f insector, a pursuing, pursuit: hostīs, L.—Fig., a railing at, deriding, abuse: principum, L.: insectationibus petitus, Ta.

insectator.definition: īnsectātor ōris, m insector, a persecutor: plebis, L.

insector.definition: īnsector ātus, arī, dep. freq. insequor, to pursue, follow up: exercitum: herbam rastris, i. e. extirpate, V.—Fig., of speech, to pursue, attack, rail at, inveigh against: ultro Insectere velut melior? lecture, H.: et…

insenesco.definition: īn-senēscō nuī, —, ere, inch, to grow old in, spend a life upon: libris, H.: malis, O.

insepultus.definition: īn-sepultus adj., unburied: acervi civium: membra, H.: insepultos proiecit, L.: sepultura, without funeral rites.

insequens.definition: īnsequēns entis, adj. P. of insequor, following, next: annus, Cs.: dies, L.

insequor.definition: īn-sequor cūtus (quūtus), ī, dep., to follow, follow after, come next: huic, V.: Orphea, H.: fugientem lumine pinum, keep in view, O.—In time, to follow, succeed: hunc proximo saeculo: mea quem aetas Insequitur, appro…

insero1.definition: īn-serō sēvī, situs, ere, to implant, ingraft: piros, V.: fissā modo cortice virgam Inserit, O.: ramos, H.: videmus insita mā la Ferre pirum, V.— Fig., to implant, ingraft, fix: num qua tibi vitiorum inseverit olim Na…

insero2.definition: īn-serō seruī, sertus, ere, to put in, introduce, insert, thrust: caput in lecticam: insertae fenestrae, V.: trecentos (in navem), H.: oculos in pectora, O.: caput in tentoria, L.: falces insertae longuriis, Cs.: subt…

inserto.definition: īnsertō —, —, āre, freq. 2 insero, to put in, insert: clipeo sinistram Insertabam aptans, V.

inservio.definition: īn-serviō —, ītus, ēre, to be serviceable, be devoted, be submissive, serve: filium amico Video inservire, T.: plebi, cui inservitum erat, the utmost deference had been shown, L.: suis commodis, attend: temporibus cal…

insibilo.definition: īn-sībilō —, —, āre, to whistle within: ubi insibilat Eurus, O.

insideo.definition: īnsideō sēdī, —, ēre 1 in+sedeo, to sit upon, settle on: equo, L.: ubi Gens iugis insedit Etruscis, V.—Fig., to take place, settle, be fixed, adhere: cum in locis semen insedit: ut in animo crimen insideret: nunc insi…

insidiae.definition: īnsidiae ārum, f SED-, a snare, trap: non lupus insidias explorat, V.: caprum Excipere insidiis, V.—In war, an ambush, ambuscade: signa aenea in insidiis ponere: insidias intravisse, Cs.: eius vitae a me insidiae posi…

insidians.definition: (īnsidiāns, ntis) m P. of insidior, a waylayer, man in ambush.— Only plur., S.

insidiator.definition: īnsidiātor ōris, m insidior, one who lies in wait, a lurker, waylayer: in foro conlocatur: eius (imperi), N.: insidiatores Massivae parare, S.

insidior.definition: īnsidior ātus, ārī, dep. insidiae, to lie in ambush, lie in wait for: ex occulto, Cs.: mihi: dolis vitae suae, S.: lupus insidiatus ovili, V.: in legatis insidiandis.—Fig., to watch for, plot against, seize stealthily…

insidiose.definition: īnsidiōsē adv. with sup. insidiosus, cunningly deceitfully, insidiously: redire: me insidiosissime tractavit.

insidiosus.definition: īnsidiōsus adj. with comp. insidiae, cunning, deceitful, treacherous, dangerous: leno, H.: quis insidiosior (est)?: sermo.

insido.definition: īn-sīdō sēdī, sessus, ere, to sit in, settle on: apes floribus insidunt, V.: insedit vapor Apuliae, H.: credit digitos insidere membris, sink into, O. —To occupy, keep possession of: silvis, V.: inscia Insidat quantus…

insigne.definition: īnsīgne is, n insignis, a mark, indication, proof, sign, token, signal: quod erat insigne, eum facere, etc.: Minerva singulare est insigne eius gymnasi: clipei insigne decorum, i. e. conspicuous shield, V.: maeroris, …

insignio.definition: īnsīgniō (imperf. īnsīgnībat, V.), ī vī, ītus, īre insignis, to mark, make conspicuous, distinguish: clipeum Auro, V.: tropaeis agros, V.: cum annus funeribus insigniretur, was remarkable for, Ta.

insignis.definition: īnsīgnis e, adj. with comp. 1 in+signum, distinguished by a mark, remarkable, noted, eminent, distinguished, prominent, extraordinary: alae, V.: vestis, L.: insigniora monumenta, L.: virtus: vis: studium erga me: insi…

insignite.definition: īnsīgnītē adv. with comp. insignitus, remarkably, extraordinarily, notably: improbus: insignitius probari, L.

insigniter.definition: īnsīgniter adv. with comp. insignis, remarkably, extraordinarily, notably: amicos diligere: in signius ornari, N.

insignitus.definition: īnsīgnītus adj. with comp. P. of insignis, marked, clear, plain: utendum imaginibus insignitis: notae veritatis.—Distinguished, striking, remarkable, notable: ignominia insignitior, L.: lacūs nomen insignitius, L.: in…

insilio.definition: īnsiliō uī (īnsilīvī, L.), —, ī re 1 in+salio, to leap in, spring up, throw oneself upon, bound, mount: huc, O.: in equum, L.: in phalangas, Cs.: undas, O.: Aetnam, H.: prorae, O.: tergo centauri, O.

insimulatio.definition: īnsimulātiō (insimil-) ōnis, f insimulo, a charge, accusation: probrorum: criminis.

insimulo.definition: īn-simulō āvī, ātus, āre, to make suspected, charge, accuse, blame, impeach: tu me insimulas, bring a charge against: Criminibus virum, O.: vilicus cum impulso tuo insimulatus esset: insimulatus falso crimine senatus,…

insincerus.definition: īn-sincērus adj., spoiled, corrupted: cruor, V.

insinuatio.definition: īnsinuātiō ōnis, f insinuo.—In rhet., a conciliation of favor, insinuating style.

insinuo.definition: īn-sinuō āvī, ātus, āre, to thrust in, push in, make a way: potestas in forum insinuandi: quācumque data intervalla essent, insinuabant ordines suos, pushed forward their files, L.—With pron reflex., to find a way in,…

insipiens.definition: īnsipiēns entis, adj. with comp. 2 in + sapiens, unwise, foolish: fortunatus: ego insipientior quam illi ipsi.

insipienter.definition: īnsipienter adv. insipiens, unwisely, foolishly: sperare.

insipientia.definition: īnsipientia ae, f insipiens, unwisdom, folly: animi.

insisto.definition: īn-sistō stitī, —, ere, to set foot, take a stand, stand on, step on, tread on: firmiter, hold their ground, Cs.: ut proximi iacentibus insisterent, stepped upon, Cs.: vestigiis abeuntium, L.: huic (saxo) institerat f…

insitio.definition: īnsitiō ōnis, f 1 in+1 SA-, an ingrafting, grafting: delectant insitiones.—The time of grafting, O.

insitivus.definition: īnsitīvus adj. insitus, ingrafted, grafted: pira, H.—Fig.: Gracchus, pretended: disciplinae, imported: liberi, spurious, Ph.

insitor.definition: insitor ōris, m 1 SA-, an ingrafter, Pr.

insitus.definition: īnsitus adj. P. of 1 insero, ingrafted, grafted: mala, V.—Fig., implanted, inborn, innate, fixed: deorum cognitiones: penitus opinio: vis, H.: menti cognitionis amor: feritas, L.

insociabilis.definition: īn-sociābilis e, adj., without social ties, not to be bound in friendship, unsociable: gens, L.: homines omni generi humano, L.

insolabiliter.definition: īnsōlābiliter adv. solor, inconsolably: dolens, H.

insolens.definition: īn-solēns ntis, adj., unaccustomed, unusual, not used, contrary to custom: Quid tu Athenas insolens? T.: aspera aequora Emirabitur insolens, H.: in dicendo, inexperienced: infamiae: belli, Cs. —Excessive, immoderate, …

insolenter.definition: īnsolenter adv. with comp. insolens, unusually, contrary to custom: evenire.—Immoderately, haughtily, insolently: laete atque insolenter ferre, with insolent exultation: hostis nostros insequens, Cs.: se insolentius i…

insolentia.definition: īnsolentia ae, f insolens, unusualness, strangeness, novelty: fori iudiciorumque: itineris, S.: voluptatum.—Of language, novelty, strangeness, affectedness: orationis: verborum.—Want of moderation, haughtiness, arroga…

insolesco.definition: īn-solēscō —, —, ere, inch, to grow haughty, become elated: per licentiam animus insolescit, S.: rebus secundis, Ta.

insolidus.definition: īn-solidus adj., not solid, tender: herba, O.

insolitus.definition: īn-solitus adj., unaccustomed, unused, unfamiliar, strange: feminae in virorum conventum: insolitae fugiunt in flumina phocae, i. e. contrary to their custom, V.: ad laborem, Cs.: rerum bellicarum, S.: eius tumultūs e…

insomnia.definition: īnsomnia ae, f insomnis, sleeplessness, want of sleep, watching: te adiget horsum insomnia, T.: insomniis fatigari, S.: insomniis carere.

insomnis.definition: īnsomnis e, adj. 2 in + somnus, sleepless, wakeful: ille noctes insomnis agit, H.: draco, O.: nox, V.

insomnium1.definition: īnsomnium ī, n 1 in+somnus, a dream. —Sing., Ta.— Plur., T., V., Tb.

insomnium2.definition: īnsomnium ī, n 2 in+somnus, sleeplessness.—Only plur: insomnia portare ocellis, Pr.

insono.definition: īn-sonō uī, —, āre, to resound: Boreae cum spiritus Insonat Aegaeo, roars over, V.: caeli delapsa per auras Insonuit, resounded, V.: pennis, rustle with, O.: calamis, make music with, O.: insonuitque flagello, cracked…

insons.definition: īn-sōns ntis, adj., guiltless, innocent: amicus, V.: publici consili, L.: si regni crimine insons fuerit, L.—As subst m.: insontes sicuti sontes circumvenire, S.—Harmless: Cerberus, H.: casa, O.

insopitus.definition: īn-sōpītus adj., sleepless, wakeful: draco, O.

inspecto.definition: (īnspectō —, —, āre), freq. inspicio, to look at, observe, view.—Only P. praes.: ipsis inspectantibus, before their very eyes: inspectante exercitu: inspectante ipso, Cs.

insperans.definition: (īnspērāns, ntis) adj., not hoping, not expecting.— Only dat. and abl: salutem insperantibus reddere, beyond their hope: insperante hoc atque invito Pamphilo, against the hope and wish, T.

insperatus.definition: īn-spērātus adj., unhoped for, unlooked for, unexpected, unforeseen: gaudium, T.: praesidium: tellus, V.: pluma, unwelcome, H.: omnibus consilium: nihil tam insperatum accidere potuit, L.— As subst n.: ex insperato, u…

inspergo.definition: īnspergō spersī, spersus, ere 1 in+spargo, to sprinkle over, scatter: molam ac vinum: inspersos reprehendas corpore naevos, H.

inspicio.definition: īnspiciō spēxī, spectus, ere 1 in+specio, to look into, look upon, inspect, consider, contemplate, examine, survey: in vitas omnium, T.: cupiditas inspiciendi: cum Romam inspexerit Eos, O.: urbīs, H.: ranarum viscera,…

inspico.definition: īnspīcō —, —, ere spica, to cut in the form of an ear of corn, sharpen: ferro faces, V.

inspiro.definition: īn-spīrō āvī, ātus, āre, to blow upon, breathe into, inspire: conchae, O.: Se (Fames) viro inspirat, O.—Fig., to inspire, excite, inflame: occultum ignem, V: animas, O.—To instil, implant: venenum Morsibus, V.: virus,…

inspoliatus.definition: īn-spoliātus adj., not plundered, not made spoil: arma, V.

instabilis.definition: īn-stabilis e, adj., not steadfast, unsteady, unstable, tottering, not firm: ingressus, L.: cymbae, V.: naves, Cu.: acies, shaken, L.—Giving no support: tellus, O.—Fig., unstable, inconstant, changeable, fickle: insta…

instans.definition: īnstāns antis, adj. with comp. P. of insto, present, immediate: quae venientia metuuntur, eadem efficiunt aegritudinem instantia: bellum. — Pressing, urgent: periculum, N.: species instantior, Ta.

instanter.definition: (īnstanter) adv., earnestly, pressingly.—Only comp: instantius concurrere, Ta.

instantia.definition: īnstantia ae, f insto, an impendence, approach: futura quorum vera erit instantia.

instar.definition: īnstar n indecl, an image, likeness, resemblance, appearance: terra quasi puncti instar obtinet, looks almost like: parvum instar eorum, quae concepisset, a small specimen, L.: omnia vix minimi momenti instar habent, …

instauratio.definition: īnstaurātiō ōnis, f instauro, a renewing, repetition: ludorum: ludi ex instauratione paran tur, L.

instaurativus.definition: īnstaurātīvus adj. instauro, instituted anew, begun afresh: ludi.

instauro.definition: īnstaurō āvī, ātus, āre, to establish, ordain: choros, V.—To renew, repeat, resume: instaurandae caedis potestas: novum de integro bellum, L.: infestis pugnam sagittis, Iu.: diem donis, celebrates with repeated offeri…

insterno.definition: īn-sternō strāvī, strātus, ere, to cover, cover over, spread upon: insternor pelle leonis, V.: pontīs altos, floored (i. e. constructed), V.: pulpita tignis, laid the stage over a scaffolding, H.

instigator.definition: īnstīgātor ōris, m instigo, a stimulator, instigator: sibi quisque, Ta.

instigatrix.definition: īnstīgātrīx īcis, f instigo, she that instigates: adversum alqm, Ta.

instigo.definition: īnstīgō āvī, ātus, āre STIG-, to goad on, urge, stimulate, stir, set on, incite, instigate: si hic non insanit satis suā sponte, instiga, T.: instigante te, at your instigation: sequentem studiis, V.: Romanos in Hanni…

instillo.definition: īn-stīllō āvī, ātus, āre, to pour in by drops, drop in, instil: lumini oleum: (oleum) caulibus, H.—To drop upon, fall on: guttae saxa instillant. —Fig., to instil, infuse: tuae litterae mihi quiddam quasi animulae ins…

instimulator.definition: īnstimulātor ōris, m instimulo, a stimulator: seditionis.

instimulo.definition: īn-stimulō —, —, āre, to goad, urge on, stimulate: Bacchas sonis, O.: Venerem verbis, O.

instinctor.definition: īnstinctor ōris, m STIG-, an instigator: sceleris, Ta.

instinctus2.definition: (īnstinctus ūs), m instinguo, instigation (only abl sing.): instinctu divino, by inspiration.

instinguo.definition: (īn-stinguō) —, stinctus, ere, to instigate, incite, impel (only P. pass.): furore et audaciā, impelled: vocibus, animated, L.: furiis, inspired, L.

instita.definition: īnstita ae, f a border, flounce of a lady's tunic: Quarum subsutā talos tegit instita veste, H.: longa, O.: nulla, i. e. no lady, O.

institi.definition: īnstitī. I. Perf. of insisto.—II. Perf. of insto.

institio.definition: īnstitiō ōnis, f STA-, a standing still: stellarum.

institor.definition: īnstitor ōris, m STA-, a factor, broker, huckster, hawker, peddler: chirographorum: amata multum institoribus, H.: ipse mercis, peddler of his own wares, L.: hibernae tegetis, Iu.

instituo.definition: īnstituō uī, ūtus, ere 1 in+statuo, to put in place, plant, fix, set: vestigia nuda sinistri pedis, V.: hominem in animum, i. e. to set one's heart on, T.—Of troops, to draw up, arrange: duplici acie institutā , Cs.: …

institutio.definition: īnstitūtiō ōnis, f instituo, disposition, arrangement: rerum: institutionem suam conservare, custom.—Instruction, education: doctoris: de aliquā re: Graecis institutionibus eruditi, learning.

institutum.definition: īnstitūtum ī, n P. of instituo, a purpose, intention, design: consulatūs tui: pauca de instituto meo dicere: huius libri.— A practice, custom, usage, habit: hi linguā, institutis differunt, Cs.: meretricium: utor inst…

insto.definition: īn-stō stitī, statūrus, āre, to stand upon, take a position: iugis, V.—To draw nigh, approach, be at hand, impend: partus instabat prope, T.: nox instabat, S.: ea quae videntur instare: instant ludi: cum illi iter ins…

instratus2.definition: īn-strātus adj., not covered: cubile, unspread, V.

instrenuus.definition: īn-strēnuus adj., sluggish, spiritless: animus, T.

instrepo.definition: īn-strepō uī, itus, ere, to resound, rattle, creak: sub pondere faginus axis Instrepat, V.

instringo.definition: (īn-stringō) —, ictus, ere, to bind, fasten.— — Only P. pass.: Instricta fides gemmis, inlaid, O.

instructe.definition: (īnstrūctē) adv., with great preparation.— Only comp: ludos instructius facere, L.

instructio.definition: īnstrūctiō ōnis, f STRV-, an array: instructione aspectuque signorum pulsus.

instructor.definition: īnstrūctor ōris, m instruo, a preparer: convivi.

instructus1.definition: īnstrūctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of instruo, furnished, provided, supplied: domicilia rebus iis, etc.: instructae ornataeque naves: decem vitiis instructior, H.—Fig., arranged, prepared, ready: in corde consilia…

instructus2.definition: (īnstrūctus, ūs) m STRV-, arrangement, preparation.— Only abl sing.: oratio eodem instructu comitata.

instrumentum.definition: īnstrūmentum ī, n STRV-, an implement, utensil, tool, instrument: tela et cetera instrumenta militiae, S.: crudelia instrumenta necis, O.—Collect. in sing, instruments, apparatus, material, stock, furniture: instrumen…

instruo.definition: īn-struō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to build in, insert: Eam (contabulationem) in parietes, Cs.—Of troops, to form, set in order, draw up, array: ad instruendum spatium, L.: hosce, T.: exercitum, S.: aciem: aciem instructum hab…

insuavis.definition: īn-suāvis e, adj. with comp. and sup, unpleasant, disagreeable: vita: haberi, H.: insuavissima littera.

insudo.definition: īn-sūdō —, —, āre, to sweat on, stain with sweat: quīs (libellis) manus insudet volgi, H.

insuefactus.definition: īnsuēfactus adj. insuesco + facio, accustomed, habituated (adsuetus): equi, Cs.

insuesco.definition: īn-suēscō suēvī (-suērat, Ta.), suē tus, ere, to habituate oneself, become accustomed, be inured: mentiri, T.: amare, S.: militem victoriā frui, L.— To accustom, habituate: hoc me Ut fugerem, H.: ita se a pueris insue…

insuetus.definition: īn-suētus adj. P. of insuesco, unaccustomed, unused, inexperienced: contumeliae: huius generis pugnae, Cs.: navigandi, Cs.: male audiendi, N.: vera audire, L.: acies inferre pedestrīs, V.: miratur nemus insuetum Scuta…

insula.definition: īnsula ae, f 1 SAL-, an island, isle: Delos: Rheni amnis, Ta.— A part of Rome encircled by the Tiber, O.—A part of Syracuse cut off by an arm of the sea, L., C.—An enclosed court, tenement for poor families: Clodi.

insulanus.definition: īnsulānus ī, m insula, an islander.

insulse.definition: īnsulsē adv. insulsus, tastelessly, insipidly, foolishly, absurdly: omnia fieri: non insulse interpretari, not without wit.

insulsitas.definition: īnsulsitās ātis, f insulsus, tastelessness, insipidity, silliness, want of wit: eorum: harum rerum: orationis.

insulsus.definition: īnsulsus adj. with sup. 2 in+salsus, unsalted, without taste, coarse: gula.—Fig., bungling, awkward: bipennis, Iu.—Tasteless, insipid, silly, absurd: Fatuos est, insulsus, T.: in verbo non insulsum genus (ridiculi): a…

insulto.definition: īnsultō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. insilio, to spring at, leap upon, leap, bound, jump, spring: fremit aequore toto Insultans sonipes, V.: busto, H.: Fluctibus insultavere carinae, O.: istas (forīs) calcibus, T.: nemora av…

insum.definition: īn-sum īnfuī, inesse, to be in, be upon: ibi inerat pictura (i. e. in conclavi), T.: Hic . . . minotaurus inest, V.: in urbe: quae (fercula) inerant canistris, H.: inerant lunaria fronti Cornua, O.— Fig., to be contai…

insumo.definition: īn-sūmō sūmpsī, sūmptus, ere, to take for, apply, expend: ut nullus teruncius insumatur in quemquam: non est melius quo insumere possis, H.: Nullum ultra verbum, quin amares, etc., waste no word, to hinder, etc., H.—F…

insuo.definition: īn-suō uī, ūtus, ere, to sew in, sew into, sew up: insutus in culeum: terga boum plumbo insuto, i. e. the cestus, V.: patrio (infans) Insuitur femori, O.: insutum vestibus aurum, embroidered, O.

insuper.definition: īn-super adv., above, on the top, overhead: insuper bipedalibus trabibus immissis, Cs.: montīs insuper altos Imposuit, V.: cumulatis in aquas sarcinis, insuper incumbebant, L.: circumvelari, O.—From above: iugum insup…

insuperabilis.definition: īn-superābilis e, adj., that cannot be passed over, insurmountable: Alpium transitus, L.—Invincible: genus bello, V.—Inevitable: fatum, O.

insurgo.definition: īn-surgō surrēxī, surrēctus, ere, to rise up, rise, lift oneself: attolli et insurgere, Ta.: (serpens) arduus insurgens, V.: Altior insurgens heros, V.: Ostendit dextram insurgens Entellus (for the blow), V.: insurgit…

insusurro.definition: īn-susurrō āvī, ātus, āre, to whisper to, insinuate, suggest: alteri: ad aurem familiariter: in aurem: mihi cantilenam: navigandi nobis tempus esse.

intabesco.definition: in-tābēscō buī, —, ere, inch, to waste away, pine away: cum semel fixae cibo Intabuissent pupulae, H.: videndo, to pine with envy, O.—To melt away, dissolve: ut intabescere Igne cerae solent, O.

intactus.definition: in-tāctus adj. with comp, untouched, uninjured, intact: cervix iuvencae, not broken to the yoke, V.: boves, H.: nix, L.: exercitus, L.: intactis adsidere muris, L.: nemo intactus profugit, S.: Britannus, unsubdued, H.…

intaminatus.definition: intāminātus adj. TAG-, unsullied, undefiled: honores, H.

intectus2.definition: in-tēctus adj., uncovered, unclad: cetera intecti, with no other covering, Ta.—Unconcealed, frank, Ta.

integellus.definition: 'integellus adj. dim. integer, pretty safe, in fair condition: alqm praestare: alqd, Ct.'

integer.definition: integer tegra, tegrum, adj. with comp. integrior and sup. integerrimus 2 in-+TAG-, untouched, unhurt, entire, whole, complete: annus: integro die, i. e. with the day before us, H.: quarum (sublicarum) pars inferior in…

intego.definition: in-tegō tēxī, tēctus, ere, to cover over: reliqua pars scrobis virgultis integebatur, Cs.: cum primā luce densa nebula saltum intexit, L.—To protect: vidit vallo etiam integi Romanos, L.

integrasco.definition: integrāscō —, —, ere, inch. integro, to begin anew, break out afresh: hoc malum integrascit, T.

integratio.definition: integrātiō ōnis, f integro, a renewing, restoring: Amantium irae amoris integratio, T.

integre.definition: integrē adv. integer, purely, correctly: dicere.—Fig., irreproachably, honestly, without prejudice: iudicare: avaritiam alcuis mutare, Ta.: ubi integre egit, disinterestedly, Ta.

integritas.definition: integritās ātis, f integer, completeness, soundness: corporis: valetudinis.—Fig., purity, correctness: Latini sermonis.—Blamelessness, innocence, integrity: vitae, S.: integritas atque innocentia: vitae, N.: mulierem …

integro.definition: integrō āvī, ātus, āre integer, to make whole: artūs in pravum elapsos, i. e. set, Ta.—To renew, begin again: lacrimas, L.: carmen, V.—Fig., to recreate, refresh: animus admiratione integratur.

integumentum.definition: integumentum ī, n intego, a covering: lanx cum integumentis, lids, L.—That which conceals, a covering: frontis: flagitiorum: nequitia frontis involuta integumentis.

intellectus2.definition: intellēctus ūs, m 1 LEG-, a perception, discernment: hiems et ver intellectum ac vocabula habent, i. e. are recognized, Ta.

intellegens.definition: intellegēns entis, adj. P. of intellego, intelligent, discerning, appreciative: vir: iudicium: dicendi existimator: cuiusvis generis: in hisce rebus, versed.

intellegentia.definition: intellegentia (intellig-) ae, f intellegens, discernment, understanding, intelligence: pars animi, intellegentiae particeps: in quibus (gustu et odoratu) est intellegentia.—Understanding, knowledge: iuris: Eam calamit…

intellego.definition: intellegō (not intelligō), ēxī (intellēxtī , T., C.; intellēgit, S.), ēctus inter+lego, to come to know, see into, perceive, understand, discern, comprehend, gather: quod ubi intellexi: id quod omnes intellegunt: cum …

intemeratus.definition: in-temerātus adj., inviolate, chaste, pure: Camilla, V.: munera, of pure wine, V.

intemperans.definition: in-temperāns antis, adj. with comp. and sup., without self-control, unrestrained, extravagant, immoderate, intemperate: intemperantis esse arbitror scribere, etc.: fui in te intemperantior, quam debui: in augendo eo i…

intemperanter.definition: 'intemperanter adv. with comp. intemperans, immoderately, extravagantly, intemperately: abuti otio: intemperantius opibus suis uti: aviditate caedis intemperantius secuti, too rashly, Cs.'

intemperantia.definition: intemperantia ae, f intemperans, want of moderation, excess, extravagance, intemperance: menti inimica: vini, immoderate use, L.—Arrogance, insolence, insubordination: Pausaniae, N.: suā intemperantiā, nimiāque licent…

intemperies.definition: (in-temperiēs) — (only acc. and abl.), f want of moderation, irregularity, excess, inclemency: caeli, L.: aquarum, immoderate rains, L.— Fig., of conduct, excess, outrage, fury: amici: unius: cohortium, Ta.

intempestive.definition: in-tempestīvē adv. imtempestivus, unseasonably, inappropriately: accedere: agere, L.: fovere volnera mentis, O.

intempestivus.definition: in-tempestīvus adj., untimely, unseasonable, inopportune: amicitia numquam est: Minerva, i. e. unseasonable spinning, O.: honos, Ta.

intempestus.definition: intempestus adj. 2 in+tempus, unseasonable, unpropitious, dark: nox, the dead of night.— Person.: intempesta silet Nox, dismal Night (mother of the Furies), V.—Unwholesome, unhealthy: Graviscae, V.

intemptatus2.definition: in-temptātus (intent-) adj., untouched, untried, unattempted: miseri, quibus Intemptata nites, H.: nil intemptatum linquere, H.: sors rerum, V.: iter, Ta.

intendo.definition: in-tendō dī, tus, ere, to stretch out, reach forth, extend: dextram ad statuam: manūs, O.: iubet intendi bracchia velis, V.—To stretch, spread out, lay, fasten, extend: intendentibus tenebris, spreading, L.: tabernacu…

intente.definition: (intentē) adv. with comp. intentus, with earnestness, attentively, intently.—Only comp: cum delectus intentius haberetur, L.: intentius premere obsessos, Ta.: alqm admovere ut, etc., L.

intentio.definition: intentiō ōnis, f 2 TA-, a stretching, straining, tension: corporis.— Fig., an exertion, effort, application, attention: animi: lusūs, to play, L.— A purpose, intention: adversariorum.

intento.definition: intentō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. intendo, to aim, direct, wield in hostility, stretch threateningly: dolor ardentīs faces intentat: pauci Romanum imperium intentantes, i. e. holding up as a threat, L.: haec sica intent…

intentus1.definition: intentus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of intendo, attentive, intent, waiting, eager: Romani intenti festinare, S.: milites pugnae proventum exspectabant, Cs.: intenti ora tenebant, V.: intentis oculis contemplari: in e…

intentus2.definition: intentus ūs, m 2 TA-, a stretching out: palmarum intentūs.

intepeo.definition: in-tepeō —, —, ēre, to be lukewarm: lacus, Pr.

intepesco.definition: īn-tepēscō puī, —, ere, inch, to become lukewarm, be warmed: strata membris tuis, O.— Poet.: Ut semel intepuit mucro, felt blood, V.

inter.definition: inter praep. with acc. ANA-, between, betwixt: (mons) inter Sequanos et Helvetios, Cs.: inter me et Brundisium esse.—With more than two objects, among, amid, in the midst of, surrounded by: inter hostium tela versari:…

interamenta.definition: interāmenta ōrum, n inter, the interior woodwork (of a ship of war): navium, L.

interaresco.definition: inter-ārēscō —, —, ere, inch, to become dry, dry up, decay: nihil interarescere debet.

intercalaris.definition: intercalāris e, adj. intercalo, of insertion, to be inserted, intercalary: Kalendae, of an intercalary month: Kalendae priores, of the first intercalary month (Caesar introduced two).

intercalarius.definition: intercalārius adj. intercalaris, for insertion, intercalary: mensis, L.: Kalendae, of an intercalary month, L.—As subst. (sc. mensis).

intercalo.definition: inter-calō āvī, ātus, āre, to proclaim an insertion in the calendar, insert, intercalate (a prerogative of the pontifices): ut pugnes, ne intercaletur. —To put off, postpone: intercalata poena, L.

intercapedo.definition: intercapēdō īnis, f intercapio, an interruption, interval, respite: scribendi.

intercedo.definition: inter-cēdō cessī, cessus, ere, to come between, intervene, be between: palus, quae intercedebat, Cs.: inter singulas legiones impedimentorum numerum intercedere, Cs.—To occur, happen, come to pass: neque ullam rem int…

interceptio.definition: interceptiō ōnis, f CAP-, a taking away: poculi.

interceptor.definition: interceptor ōris, m CAP-, an intercepter, usurper, embezzler: praedae, L.: donativi, Ta.

intercessio.definition: intercessiō ōnis, f 1 CAD-, a mediation, suretyship: mea intercessio parata est.—An intervention, interposition, protest, veto: tribunicia, Cs.: empta: remittere intercessionem, L.

intercessor.definition: intercessor ōris, m 1 CAD-, one who interposes, a mediator, surety: intercessorem quaerere: isto intercessore legati non adierunt, through his interference: rei malae.—An interferer, protester, adversary, preventer: s…

intercido1.definition: intercīdō īdī, īsus, ere inter+caedo, to cut asunder, divide, cut through, cut down: lacus, interciso monte, defluit: pontem, L.

intercido2.definition: intercidō idī,—,ere inter+cado, to fall between: inter arma corporaque intercidente telo, L.—To occur meanwhile, happen: si quae interciderunt, etc.—Fig., to fall to the ground, perish: pereant amici, dum unā inimici …

intercino.definition: intercinō —, —, ere inter+cano, to sing between: neu quid medios intercinat actūs, H.

intercipio.definition: intercipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere inter+capio, to seize in passing, intercept: quod nos capere oportet, T.: pila intercepta remittere, Cs.: venenum, take the poison intended for another: numerum iumentorum, Cs.: ab suis in…

intercise.definition: intercīsē adv. 1 intercido, piecemeal, interruptedly: dictum (opp. directe).

intercludo.definition: interclūdō ūsī, ūsus, ere inter+claudo, to shut out, shut off, cut off, hinder, stop, block up, intercept: virtus voluptatis aditū s intercludat necesse est: interclusis itineribus, Cs.: illos ponti Interclusit hiemps…

interclusio.definition: interclūsiō ōnis, f intercludo, a stopping, entire suspension: animae (in speaking).

intercolumnium.definition: intercolumnium ī, n inter+columna, a space between two columns, intercolumniation.

intercurro.definition: inter-currō currī, cursus, ere, to run between, intervene, mediate: qui intercurrerent, misimus trīs principes civitatis.—Of time, to hasten meanwhile: ipse interim Veios intercurrit, L.—Fig., t<*> mingle, be associat…

intercurso.definition: inter-cursō —, —, āre, freq. intercurro, to run in, intervene: intercursantibus barbaris, L.

intercursus.definition: (intercursus ūs), m 1 CEL-.—Only abl. sing, a running between, intervention, interposition: periculum intercursu filii propulsatum, L.: consulum intercursu rixa sedata est, L.

intercus.definition: 'intercus cutis, adj. inter+cutis, under the skin, intercutaneous: aqua, dropsy.'

interdico.definition: inter-dīcō dīxī, dictus, ere, to interpose by speaking, forbid, prohibit, interdict: praetor interdixit: non tulit ut interdicatur: quae interdicta sunt: interdicta voluptas, H.: Cassivellauno ne noceat, Cs.: praecipi…

interdictio.definition: interdictiō ōnis, f DIC-, a prohibiting, forbidding: aquae et ignis, banishment: finium, L.

interdictum.definition: interdictum ī, n P. of interdico, a forbiden thing: si interdicta petes, H.—A prohibition: deorum.—Of the praetor, a provisional decree, interlocutory order, prohibition, interdict: praetorum interdicta tollentur: tyr…

interdiu.definition: interdiū adv. DIV-, during the day, in the daytime, by day: nec nocte nec interdiu, L.

interductus.definition: (interductus ūs), m DVC-, interpunctuation; only abl.

interdum.definition: inter-dum adv., sometimes, occasionally, now and then: Pecuniam neglegere est interdum lucrum, T.: saepe gratiā interdum iurgiis trahendo tempus, S.: lacrimas tenere, Cs.: dicere: interdum . . . interdum, now . . . no…

interea.definition: inter-eā adv., meanwhile, in the meantime, in the interim: saepe interea mihi senex Narrabat, T.: dies advenit: quietus erat, S.: interea loci, in the meantime, T.—Meanwhile, nevertheless, however: tu interea non cess…

intereo.definition: inter-eō iī, itūrus, īre (perf. interīsse, C.), to go among, be lost: ut interit magnitudine maris stilla muriae.—Fig., to perish, go to ruin, decay, die: pauci interiere, S.: statuae intereunt tempestate: tormentorum…

interequito.definition: inter-equitō —, —, āre, to ride between: ipse interequitans, L.: ordines, L.: agmina, Cu.

interfatio.definition: interfātiō ōnis, f interfor, a speaking between, interruption.

interfector.definition: interfector ōris, m inter+2 FAC-, a slayer, murderer, assassin: eorum, C., L.

interfectrix.definition: interfectrīx īcis, f interfector, a murderess: nepotis, Ta.

interficio.definition: interficiō fēcī, fectus, ere inter+facio, to put out of the way, destroy, bring to naught: messīs, V.—To kill, slay, murder: interfici quom perpeti me possum, i. e. die willingly, T.: insidiis interfectus est: virum d…

interfluo.definition: inter-fluō —, —, ere, to flow between: quantum interfluit fretum, L.: media moenia, Cu.: Romanos Cheruscosque, Ta.

interfor.definition: inter-for ātus, ārī, dep., to interrupt in speaking: Venus sic interfata est, V.: priusquam postulatum perageret Appius interfatur, L.: Phaeneas interfatus, interrupting, L.

interfulgens.definition: inter-fulgēns P., gleaming amidst.—With dat: cumulo rerum, L. dub.

interfusus.definition: inter-fūsus adj., poured between, interposed: Dido maculis trementī s interfusa genas, stained, V.: Styx coërcet (animas), V.: interfusa nitentī s aequora Cycladas, H.

interiaceo.definition: inter-iaceō uī, —, ēre, to lie between: spatio quod vacui interiacebat campi, L.: castra Punica ac Romana interiacebat campus, L.: campus interiacens Tiberi ac moenibus Romanis, L.

intericio.definition: intericiō iēcī, iectus, ere inter+iacio, to throw between, set between, intersperse, join, intermix: legionarias intericiunt cohortes, Cs.: id interiecit inter individuum atque id, quod, etc.: his maestis laetitia int…

interiectus.definition: (interiectus ūs), m inter+IA-.—Only acc. and abl. sing, a coming between, intervention: luna interiectu terrae repente deficit.—An interval: temporis, meanwhile, Ta.: dierum, Ta.

interim.definition: interim adv. inter+old acc. from 2 I-, meanwhile, in the meantime: interim Romā subito profectus est: interim cotidie Caesar Aeduos frumentum flagitare, Cs.: interim dum, etc., T.: et tamen interim, S.—However, nevert…

interimo.definition: interimō or interemō ēmī, ēmptus, or ēmtus inter+emo, to take from the midst, take away, do away with, abolish: interimendorum sacrorum causā.—To destroy, slay, kill: interemptam oportuit, T.: plures eo proelio intere…

interior.definition: interior ius, gen. ōris inter, inner, interior, middle: aedium pars: spatium, O.: In interiore parte ut maneam, i. e. in the women's apartment, T.: domus, inner part, V.: epistula, body: motu cietur interiore et suo: …

interitio.definition: interitiō ōnis, f inter+I-, destruction, ruin: aratorum.

interitus.definition: interitus ūs, m inter+I-, overthrow, fall, ruin, destruction, annihilation: interitum rei p. lugere: familiam ab interitu vindicare: omnium rerum interitū s: exercitūs.—Death: Sabini, Cs.: voluntarius: tuum ingemuisse…

interiungo.definition: inter-iungō —, ūnctus, ere, to join together, clasp: dextrae interiunctae, L.

interius2.definition: interius adv. neut. of interior, in the inner part, on the inside, in the middle, within: oratio ne insistat interius, i. e. halt too soon: recondere, V.—Fig.: attendere, to look closely, Iu.

interlabor.definition: inter-lābor —, ī, dep., to flow between.—In tmesis: inter enim labentur aquae, percolate, V.

interlego.definition: inter-legō —, —, ere, to pluck here and there, cull.— In tmesis: Carpendae frondes, interque legendae, V.

interlino.definition: inter-linō lēvī, litus, ere, to smear between, spread between, join with: caementa luto, L.: murus bitumine interlitus, Cu.—To make erasures in, alter by erasing: testamentum.

interloquor.definition: inter-loquor locūtus, ī, dep., to interrupt in speaking: mihi, T.

interluceo.definition: inter-lūceō lūxī, —, ēre, to shine in the midst: quaedam animalia interlucent (in amber), Ta.—To lighten at intervals, shine irregularly.—Impers.: noctu interluxisse, L.—Fig., to be manifest, be plainly visible: ordin…

interlunium.definition: interlūnium ī, n interlunis, the time of new moon.—Plur., H.

interluo.definition: inter-luō —, —, ere.—Of streams, to wash under, flow between: pontus arva et urbīs interluit, V.: quosque secans interluit Allia, V.: saxa interluens unda, Cu.

intermenstruus.definition: inter-mēnstruus adj., between months: tempus, the change of moon.

interminatus.definition: in-terminātus adj., unbounded, endless: in omnīs partī s magnitudo regionum.

interminor.definition: inter-minor ātus, ārī, dep., to threaten, forbid with threats: Istucine tibi, T.: interminatus cibus, forbidden, H.

intermisceo.definition: inter-misceō miscuī, mīxtus, ēre, to mix among, intermix, mingle: turbabant equos pedites intermixti, L.: tibi undam, V.: patriis petita Verba foris, H.: intermixti hostibus cognoscunt, L.

intermissio.definition: intermissiō ōnis, f intermitto, a breaking off, intermission, interruption, discontinuance: forensis operae: sine ullā intermissione: per intermissiones has, L.: epistularum, of correspondence: verborum, i. e. abruptn…

intermitto.definition: inter-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to leave off, intermit, omit, suspend, interrupt, neglect: iter, proelium, Cs.: hoc intermisi, quoad non licuit: laborem, O.: Intermissa diu bella, H.: litteras mittere: non intermittit …

intermorior.definition: inter-morior mortuus, ī, dep., to die off, die out: intermoriuntur reliquiae coniurationis: ignis, Cu.: intermori civitatem sinere, L.: officium apud me intermoriturum, i. e. to be forgotten.

intermortuus.definition: intermortuus adj. P. of intermorior, dead, lifeless, faint: intermortuus exspiravit, fainted, L. —Fig.: contiones: memoria generis sui.

intermundia.definition: intermundia ōrum, n plur. inter+mundus, spaces between worlds.

intermuralis.definition: inter-mūrālis e, adj., between the walls: amnis, i. e. ditch, L.

internascor.definition: (inter-nāscor) nātus, ī, dep., to grow between, spring up in the way: internata virgulta, L.: internatae saxis herbae, Ta.

internecio.definition: interneciō (-niciō) ōnis, f inter+1 NEC-, a massacre, slaughter, carnage, extermination, destruction: internicione civĩs liberare: bella ad internecionem gesta, N.: ad internecionem caesi, all put to the sword, L.: ad…

internecivus.definition: internecīvus adj. internecio, murderous, destructive: bellum, of extermination, C., L.

internecto.definition: inter-nectō —, —, ere, to bind together, bind up: ut fibula crinem Auro internectat, V.

interniteo.definition: inter-niteō —, —, ēre, to shine through, shine at intervals: si qua sidera internitebant, Cu.

internodium.definition: inter-nōdium ī, n inter+nodus, the space between two joints: quā facit internodia poples, O.

internosco.definition: inter-nōscō nōvī, nōtus, ere, to know apart, distinguish, discern: fures: blandus amicus a vero internosci potest: mendacem verumque amicum, H.: visa vera sint, anne falsa.

internuntia.definition: inter-nūntia ae, f a mediator, messenger: aves internuntiae Iovis: Iudaea: caeli, Iu.

internuntio.definition: inter-nūntiō —, —, ēre, to exchange messages, negotiate: utri transgrederentur, L.

internuntius.definition: inter-nūntius ī, a mediator, messenger, gobetween: Nequis internuntius ad istam curset, T.: internuntiis ultro citroque missis, Cs.: totius rei, L.: Iovis interpretes internuntiique, i. e. the augurs.

internus.definition: internus adj. inter, inward, internal: arae, O.—Fig.: mala, domestic, S.: discordiae, Ta.

intero.definition: in-terō trīvī, trītus, ere, to rub in, crumble in. — Prov.: Tute hoc intrīsti, tibi omnest exedendum, you have your own mess to swallow, T.

interpellatio.definition: interpellatiō ōnis, f interpello, a speaking between, interruption.

interpellator.definition: interpellātor ōris, m interpello, an interrupter, disturber: se oblectare sine interpellatoribus.

interpello.definition: interpellō āvī, ātus, āre 1 PAL-, to interrupt, break in upon: interpellando trahere tempus, S.: Interpellandi locus erat, H.: alqm ingressum in sermonem, Cs.: nihil te interpellabo: ab alqo interpellari, Cu.—To urge …

interpolo.definition: interpolō āvī, ātus, āre interpolus (old), furbished, to polish, furbish, dress up: togam praetextam, dye anew.—Of writings, to interpolate, alter, falsify: aliquid.

interpono.definition: inter-pōnō posuī, posītus, ere, to put between, place among, interpose, insert, intersperse: ubi spatium . . . pilae interponuntur, Cs.: ne interpositi quidem elephanti militem deterrebant, L.: lateri vinculum lapides…

interpositio.definition: interpositiō ōnis, f interpositus, an insertion, introduction: personarum: una (of words).

interpositus2.definition: (interpositus, ūs) m interpono, a putting between, interposition.— Only abl sing.: luna interpositu terrae deficit.

interpres.definition: interpres etis, m and f PRAT-, a middleman, mediator, broker, factor, negotiator: interpretes corrumpendi iudici: pacis, L.: divūm, messenger (i. e. Mercury), V.: harum curarum Iuno, i. e. of the anxieties of love, V.…

intingo.definition: (in-tingō or in-tinguō) —, inctus, ere, to dip, soak.— Only P. perf.: intinctae (faces sanguine), O.
