invitamentum.definition: invītāmentum ī, n invito, an invitation, allurement, incitement, inducement: invitamenta urbis, attractions: (honos) non invitamentum ad tempus est: ad luxuriam, L.: temeritatis, L.

invitatio.definition: invītātiō ōnis, f invito, an invitation, incitement, challenge: fit invitatio, ut biberetur: ad dolendum: benigna, i. e. to a banquet, L.: invitationes adventūsque nostrorum hominum.

invitatus.definition: (invītātus, ūs) m invito, an inviting, invitation.— Only abl: invitatu tuo.

invite.definition: (īnvītē) adv. with comp, against one's will, unwillingly: cepi Capuam: invitius accedere.

invito.definition: invītō āvī, ātus, āre for * invocito, freq. of invoco, to invite, treat, feast, entertain: hominem, T.: suos in castra invitandi causā adducunt, for entertainment, Cs.: te domum suam: alius alium domos suas invitant, …

invitus.definition: invītus adj. with sup, against the will, unwilling, reluctant, perforce, on compulsion: Invitus feci, lex coëgit, T.: neque senatus provinciam invitus dederat, S.: invitus feci, ut, etc.: ut viatores invitos consister…

invius.definition: invius adj. 2 in+via, without a road, impassable, not to be traversed, insuperable: lustra, V.: saltūs, L.: maria Teucris, V.: virtuti nulla est via, O.: nil virtuti invium, Ta.—Plur n. as subst, impassable places: pe…

invocatus2.definition: in-vocātus adj., uncalled, without a summons: ad dormientem veniunt (imagines) invocatae.—Uninvited, without an invitation: ut mihi . . . invocato sit locus, T.: ut quos invocatos vidisset in foro, omnes devocaret, N.

invoco.definition: in-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call upon, invoke, appeal to: in pariendo Iunonem Lucinam: deos testīs, L.: agmina matrum, summon, O.—To call, name, address: quem invocant omnes Iovem: aliquem dominum, Cu.

involatus.definition: (involātus, ūs) m a flying, flight; only abl: ex alitis involatu auguror.

involito.definition: involitō —, —, āre, freq. involo, to fly over, float over: umeris involitant comae, H.

involo.definition: in-volō āvī, ātus, āre, to fly at, rush upon: in capillum, fly at his hair, T.: in possessionem, make a forcible entry.

involucrum.definition: involūcrum ī, n 3 VOL-, a wrapper, covering, case, envelope: candelabri.—Fig., a cover, mask: simulationum.

involutus.definition: involūtus adj. P. of involvo, involved, intricate, obscure: res.

involvo.definition: in-volvō vī, ūtus, ere, to roll, roll upon: Ossae involvere Olympum, V.: montes, O.: armenta secum, sweep away, V.—To roll about, wrap up, envelop, involve: Involvēre diem nimbi, V.: prodire involuto capite: sinistras…

io.definition: iō interj..—Expressing joy, ho! huzza! hurra! io triumphe! H.— In a sudden call, holla! look! quick! succurrete, io! cives, H.: io! matres, audite, V.

iocatio.definition: iocātiō ōnis, f iocor, a joking, joke, jest.

iocor.definition: iocor ātus, ārī, dep. iocus, to jest, joke: tu hanc iocari credis? T.: duplex iocandi genus: voluit Fortuna iocari, Iu.—To say in jest: haec: in faciem permulta, H.: nescio quid, Ct.

iocose.definition: iocōsē adv. with comp, jestingly, jocosely: eumque lusi iocose satis: iocosius scribere.

iocosus.definition: iocōsus adj. iocus, full of jesting, jocose, humorous, droll, facetious, sportive: Maecenas, H.: Musa, O.: res: verba, O.: furtum, H.: Nilus (i. e. of the merry Egyptians), O.

iocularis.definition: ioculāris e, adj. ioculus, facetious, jocular, laughable, droll: audacia, T.—Plur n. as subst, jests, jokes, H.

iocularius.definition: ioculārius adj. ioculus, ludicrous, droll: malum, T.

ioculator.definition: ioculātor ōris, m ioculor, a jester, joker: senex.

ioculor.definition: (ioculor) —, ārī ioculus, to jest, joke; only P. praes.: quaedam militariter ioculantes, L.

iocus.definition: iocus ī (plur. also ioca, iocorum, n), m IA-, a jest, joke: iocum movere, S.: ioci causā, for the sake of the joke: ioca atque seria cum humillimis agere, S.: seria ac iocos celebrare, L.: conviva ioco mordente facetu…

iota.definition: iōta n indec., i)w=ta, the name of the Greek i, iota: ut iota litteram tollas.

ipse.definition: ipse (old ipsus, T.), a, um, gen. ipsīus (rarely ipsius, V., disyl. T.), dat. ipsī, pron demonstr. I. In gen., to express eminence or emphasis. A. Self, in person (often rendered by an emphatic he, or by very, just, p…

ira.definition: īra ae, f anger, wrath, rage, ire, passion, indignation: irā inflammatus: Ira furor brevis est, H.: irae suae parēre, N.: irā conmotus, S.: iram in eos evomere, T.: in hostilīs domos Iram vertite, H.: quorum non suffi…

iracunde.definition: īrācundē adv. with comp. iracundus, angrily, passionately: agere cum aliquo: iracundius expostulare.

iracundia.definition: īrācundia ae, f iracundus, a proneness to anger, hasty temper, irascibility: permitto aliquid iracundiae tuae.—Anger, wrath, rage, passion, violence: prae iracundiā non sum apud me, T.: cotidie aliquid iracundiae remi…

iracundus.definition: īrācundus adj. with comp. ira, irascible, irritable, passionate, choleric, angry, ireful, easily provoked: proterve, T.: homo, Cs.: senes: leones, O.: iracundior est paulo, H.—Of things: victoria: Iracunda Iovem poner…

irascor.definition: īrāscor īrātus, ī, dep. ira, to be angry, be in a rage: minume decet, S.: numquam sapiens irascitur: Irasci celer, H.: irascens, quod, etc., O.: qui nesciat irasci, Iu.: taurus irasci in cornua discit, gather his rage…

iratus.definition: īrātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of irascor, angered, enraged, angry, violent, furious: animus, T.: nihil feci iratus, in anger: quid irati sentire possunt? in their wrath, Cs.: tibi graviter, T.: adversario iudex: …

ironia.definition: īrōnīa ae, f, ei)rwnei/a, irony: sine ullā ironiā loquor.

is.definition: is ea, id, gen. ēius (sometimes monosyl. in poetry), dat. ēī (rarely eī or monosyl. ei), pron. demonst. 2 I-. I. As a weak demonst. in simple reference.—As subst, he, she, it, the one mentioned (without emphasis): fui…

istac.definition: istāc adv. abl f. of istic, sc. viā, there, that way: Abi istac, T.—Fig., in that way, in such wise: Nequaquam istuc istac ibit; magna inest certatio, Enn. ap. C.

iste.definition: iste a, ud, gen. istīus (poet. istius, V.; istius, disyl., T.; istī , T.), pron demonstr. I. Referring to that which is at hand or present to the person addressed, this, that, he, she: At tu pol tibi istas comprimite …

isti.definition: istī old for 2 istic, there, V. (Ribb.).

istic1.definition: istic aec, oc and uc (with -ne, istucine), pron demonstr. iste+ce.— Referring to that which is at hand or related to the person addressed, that of yours, that mentioned by you: istaec res, T.: circum istaec loca commo…

istic2.definition: istīc adv., there, in that place, where you are: quid istic tibi negotist? T.: quoniam istic sedes: quocumque istic loco constitisti, L.—Herein, in this affair, on this occasion: Neque istic, neque alibi, T.: Istic su…

istinc.definition: 'istinc adv. iste, from there, thence, from where you are: istinc excludere, T.: qui istinc veniunt: Fare age iam istinc, i. e. without moving, V.: si istinc fraus et audacia est, hinc pudor, on the other side . . . o…

isto.definition: istō adv. iste, thither, to you, to where you are: si minima causa est properandi isto mihi.— Thereinto, in that matter: Trabatium isto admiscere.

istoc.definition: istōc adv. istic, thither, that way, yonder: accede illuc; Nimium istoc abisti, T.

istuc.definition: istūc adv. istic, thither, to you, to where you are, in that direction: Concede istuc paululum, T.: istuc sunt delapsi: istuc mens animusque Fert, H.— To that thing, to that subject: istuc ibam, T.

ita.definition: ita adv. 2 I-. I. In gen., referring to what precedes, in this manner, in this wise, in such a way, so, thus, accordingly, as has been said: des operam ut investiges sitne ita: Ita aiunt, T.: his rebus ita actis, S.: …

itaque.definition: ita-que conj, and so, and thus, and accordingly: Si cetera ita sunt ut vis, itaque ut esse ego illa existumo, T.: ita constitui, itaque feci.—In inference, and so, accordingly, therefore, for that reason, consequently…

item.definition: item adv., likewise, besides, also, further, moreover, too, as well: Unus et item alter, T.: Lentulus, itemque ceteri, S.: Romulus augur cum fratre item augure: Contemplator item, cum, etc., V.— In the phrase, non ite…

iter.definition: iter itineris, n I-, a going, walk, way: dicam in itinere, on the way, T.— A going, journey, passage, march, voyage: cum illi iter instaret et subitum et longum: ut in itinere copia frumenti suppeteret, Cs.: in ipso i…

iteratio.definition: iterātiō ōnis, f itero, a repetition: verborum.

itero.definition: iterō āvī, ātus, āre iterum, to do a second time, repeat: cum duplicantur iteranturque verba: saepe eadem, L.: iterata pugna, renewed, L.: ubi Phoebus iteraverit ortūs, has risen a second time, O.: cursū s relictos, H…

iterum.definition: iterum adv., again, a second time, once more, anew: huc revorti iterum, T.: duxit iterum uxorem: Lepidus, imperator iterum: Pennus, iterum (consul), L.: bis rem p. servavi, semel gloriā, iterum aerumnā meā: cum his se…

itidem.definition: 'itidem adv. ita, in like manner, so, just, in the same way: tibi quae dixi, dicam itidem illi, T.: temperantia in suas itidem res, et in communes distributa est: itidem in hac re, ut in aliis, T.'

itio.definition: itiō ōnis, f I-, a going, walking, travelling: itiones crebrae, T.: reditum ac domum itionem dari.

ito.definition: itō —, —, āre, freq. eo, to go: ad cenas.

itus.definition: itus ūs, m I-, a going away, departure: noster.

iuba.definition: iuba ae, f DIV-, a mane, flowing hair on the neck: equus ille iubam quatiens, C. poët.: iubae equorum, Cs.: luduntque iubae, etc., V.: equinae, O.— A crest: triplici crinita iubā galea, V.: iubas Divini adsimulat capi…

iubar.definition: iubar arīs, n DIV-, radiance, light, splendor, brightness, sunshine: iubare exorto, V.: Quintus nitidum iubar extulit Lucifer, O.: Hanc animam, Fac iubar, i. e. make into a constellation, O.

iubatus.definition: iubātus adj. iuba, crested: anguis, L.

iubeo.definition: iubeō iussī (iūsti, for iussistī, T.; iūssō , for iusserō, V.; iūsse, for iussisse, T.), iūssus, ēre, to order, give an order, bid, tell, command: iubesne? iubeo, cogo, T.: non iubeo: defessa iubendo, O.: sic iubeo, s…

iucunde.definition: iūcundē (iōc-) adv. with comp. and sup. iucundus, agreeably, delightfully: vivere: cenam producere, H.: bibere iucundius: iucundissime vivere.

iucunditas.definition: iūcunditās (iōc-) ātis, f iucundus, agreeableness, pleasantness, delight, enjoyment: agri: epistula plena iucunditatis: dare se iucunditati, to enjoyment: ea est in homine iucunditas, ut, cheerfulness: plurimae tuae i…

iucundus.definition: iūcundus (iōc-) adj. with comp. and sup. DIV-, pleasant, agreeable, delightful, pleasing: est mihi iucunda vestra erga me voluntas: id vero militibus fuit iucundum, Cs.: praemia, H.: Crispi iucunda senectus (i. e. sen…

iudex.definition: iūdex icis, m and f ius+DIC-, a judge, juror: verissimus: nequam et levis: severissimi atque integerrimi: te ipsum habebo iudicem: quem si ferrem iudicem, proposed: ferre Volscio iudicem, L.: iudicem dicere, i. e. sub…

iudicatio.definition: iūdicātiō ōnis, f iudico, a judging, investigating: Longi subselli.—A judicial examination: Iudicatio est, etc.—Fig., a judgment, opinion: iudicatio se scire quod nesciat.

iudicatum.definition: iūdicātum ī, n P. n. of iudico, a decision, judgment, decree: iudicatum facere, to carry out. —An award, fine: solvere.

iudicatus1.definition: iūdicātus adj. P. of iudico, decided, determined: res iudicata, a precedent: infirmatio rerum iudicatarum.—As subst, a condemned person: iudicatum duci.

iudicatus2.definition: iūdicātus ūs, m iudico, a judgeship, office of judge: isti ordini iudicatus non patebit.

iudicialis.definition: iūdiciālis e, adj. iudicium, of a court of justice, judicial: ius: tabella: genus (dicendi), juridical pleading.

iudiciarius.definition: iūdiciārius adj. iudicium, of the courts, judiciary: lex: quaestus: controversia.

iudicium.definition: iūdicium ī, n iudex, a judgment, judicial investigation, trial, legal process, sentence: omnia iudicia reperta sunt, etc.: dignitatis meae, concerning: de meā fide: inter sicarios, for assassination: vocare in iudiciu…

iudico.definition: iūdicō āvī, ātus, āre iudex, to examine judicially, judge, be a judge, pass judgment, decide: cum magistratus iudicassit: ordo alius ad res iudicandas postulatur: iudicandi potestas, jurisdiction: iudicantem vidimus A…

iugalis.definition: iugālis e, adj. iugum, of a yoke, yoked together: equi iumentaque, Cu.—Plur m. as subst, a team: gemini, V.—Matrimonial, nuptial: ne cui me vinclo sociare iugali, V.: dona, O.

iugatio.definition: iugātiō ōnis, f iugo, a binding.

iugatus.definition: iugātus adj. P. of iugo, connected, dependent: virtutes inter se: verba, kindred.

iugerum.definition: iūgerum ī, n gen plur. iūgerūm; dat. and abl. iū geribus, n IV-, an acre, juger (containing 28,000 square feet): decumanum: quaterna in singulos iugera, Cs.: nescio quotenorum iugerum: per tota novem iugera Porrigitur…

iugis1.definition: iūgis e, adj. IV-, joined together: auspicium, i. e. of a yoke of oxen.

iugis2.definition: iūgis e, adj. VIV-, fresh, living, perennial: putei: aqua, S., H.

iuglans.definition: iūglāns glandis, f Iovis+glans, a walnut, walnut-tree: iuglandium putamina.

iugo.definition: iugō āvī, ātus, āre iugum, to bind, marry: alcui intactam, V.: decreta super iugandis Feminis, H.

iugosus.definition: iugōsus adj. iugum, mountainous: silvae, O.

iugulo.definition: iugulō āvī, ātus, āre iugulum, to cut the throat, kill, slay, murder: finis iugulandi, S.: civīs iugulari iussit: homines, H.: tum rite sacratas In flammam iugulant pecudes, slaughter and throw, V.— Fig., to destroy, …

iugulum.definition: iugulum ī, n (iugulus, ī, m, Iu.), dim. iugum, the collar-bone, hollow part of the neck: iugula concava habere.—The throat, neck: mucrones a iugulis vestris deiecimus: recludere stricto ense, O.: iugulos aperire susur…

iugum.definition: iugum ī, n IV-, a yoke, collar: in iugo insistere, Cs.: bestiis iuga imponimus: (bos) iuga detractans, V.: iuga demere Bobus, H.—A yoke, pair, team: ut minus multis iugis ararent: inmissa iuga, pair of horses, V.: cur…

iumentum.definition: iūmentum ī, n IV-, a beast for hauling, draught-animal, beast of burden, horse, mule, ass: iumenta onerat, S.: iumento nihil opus est (i. e. equo): sarcinaria, beasts of burden, Cs.: servi ut taceant, iumenta loquentu…

iunceus.definition: iunceus adj. iuncus, made of rushes: vincula, O.—Fig., slim, slender: alquam reddunt iunceam, T.

iuncosus.definition: iuncōsus adj. iuncus, full of rushes: litora, O.

iunctio.definition: iūnctiō ōnis, f IV-, a joining, uniting.

iunctura.definition: iūnctūra ae, f IV-, a joining, uniting, juncture, joint: tignorum, Cs.: iuncturae verticis, sutures, O.: laterum iuncturas fibula mordet, the united ends of the girdle, V.—Fig., a connection: generis, i. e. consanguin…

iunctus.definition: iūnctus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of iungo, united, connected, associated, kindred: iunctis Frontibus, in a line, V.: Per dies et iunctas noctīs, following, O.: causa cum exitu iunctior: iunctissimus illi comes, mos…

iuncus.definition: iuncus ī, m a rush: Limosus, V.: acutā cuspide iunci, O.

iungo.definition: iungō ūnxī, ūnctus, ere IV-, to join together, unite, connect, attach, fasten, yoke, harness: Narcissum et florem anethi, V.: ostia, shut, Iu.: iunctas quatere fenestras, H.: oscula, exchange, O.: da iungere dextram, …

iuniperus.definition: iūniperus ī, f the juniper-tree, V.

iurator.definition: iūrātor ōris, m iuro, a swearer, assistant of the censor, sworn census-clerk, L.

iuratus.definition: iūrātus adj. P. of iuror, sworn, under oath, bound by an oath: qui iuratus apud vos dixit: homines, jurors: testis, Iu.: in eadem arma, O.— As subst m.: huius iurati testimonium, witness.— As subst n.: iurata, solemn …

iurgium.definition: iūrgium ī, n ius+1 AG-, a quarrel, strife, dispute, altercation, contention: inde ad iurgium, T.: iurgiis trahendo tempus, S.: benevolorum concertatio iurgium dicitur: iurgia iactare, quarrel, V.: vicina refugere iurg…

iurgo.definition: iūrgō āvī, ātus, āre * iūrigus; IV-, to quarrel, brawl, dispute, scold: Cedo, quid iurgabit tecum? T.: iurgare vicinos, non litigare: haec iurgans agebat, with expostulation, L.: istis Iurgatur verbis, is reproached, H.

iuridicialis.definition: iūridiciālis e, adj. iuridicus, relating to right, of justice: genus: quaestio.

iuris1.definition: iūris cōnsultus a lawyer; see consultus.

iuris3.definition: iūris perītus learned in the law; see peritus.

iuro.definition: iūrō āvī, ātus, āre 2 ius, to swear, take an oath: si aram tenens iuraret: ex animi tui sententiā, without reservation: Boeotum in crasso iurares aëre natum, H.: falsum, swear falsely: vere: testari deos per quos iura…

iuror.definition: (iūror ātus, ārī,) dep., see iuro and iuratus.

ius.definition: iūs iūrandum (often as one word, iūsiūr-), iuris iurandi, an oath: Dabo ius iurandum nil esse, T.: ad ius iurandum popularīs adigere, S.: idem ius iurandum adigit Afranium, made him take, Cs.: iure iurando civitatem o…

ius1.definition: iūs iūris, n IV-, broth, soup, sauce: hesternum, T.: fervens: tepidum, H.—In a pun: Verrinum, hog-broth (the justice of Verres).

ius2.definition: iūs iūris (dat. iūre, L.; plur. only nom. and acc.), n IV-, that which is binding, right, justice, duty: ius hominum situm est in societate, etc.: obtinere, maintain: de iure alicui respondere, lay down the law: clien…

iussum.definition: iūssum ī, n P. neut. of iubeo, an order, command, ordinance, law: deorum immortalium iussa: iussis vostris oboediens, S.: horrida iussa, V.: iussis carmina coepta tuis, V.: efficere, execute, S.: capessere, accept, V.…

iussus2.definition: (iūssus, ūs) m an order, command, decree, ordinance (only abl sing.): vestro iussu coactus: lecti iussu populi, L.: sine populi iussu, S.: dei, V.: Neronis, Iu.

iuste.definition: iūstē adv. with comp. and sup. iustus, rightly, justly, equitably, duly: accusare: Ambo miseri, sed iustius illa, with better cause, O.: ornare hunc iustissime.

iustificus.definition: iūstificus adj. iustus+2 FAC-, that acts justly: mens deorum, Ct.

iustitia.definition: iūstitia ae, f iustus, justice, equity, righteousness, uprightness: labore atque iustitiā res p. crevit, S.: summa hominis: erga deos.— Person., V.: potens, H.—Clemency, compassion: pro eius iustitiā impetrare, Cs.: t…

iustitium.definition: iūstitium n 2 ius+STA-, a suspension of the courts, judicial vacation, holiday: iustitium edici oportere: quadriduum, L.: iustitium remittitur, L.— A public mourning, Ta.

iustus.definition: iūstus adj. with comp. and sup. 2 ius, just, upright, righteous: iudex: in socios: qui omnium iustissimus fuisse traditur.—In accordance with law, right, equitable, just: lex: supplicia: bella, O.: iustissimos triumph…

iuvenalis.definition: iuvenālis e, adj. iuvenis, youthful, juvenile, suitable for young people: amor, V.: ludus, L.: anni, O.—Plur n. as subst, youthful games, Ta.

iuvenaliter.definition: iuvenāliter adv. iuvenalis, in a youthful manner, youthfully: Iecit aurum, O.—Rashly, improvidently, O.

iuvenca.definition: iuvenca ae, f iuvencus, a young cow, heifer: formosa, V.: votiva, H.— A girl: Graia, i. e. Helen, O.: tua, H.

iuvencus.definition: iuvencus ī, m iuvenis, a young bullock: aratra iugo referunt suspensa iuvenci, V.: fessi iuvenci, O.: Te suis matres metuunt iuvencis young men, H.

iuvenesco.definition: iuvenēscō —, —, ere, inch. iuvenis, to attain youth, grow up: vitulus . . . largis iuvenescit herbis, H.—To grow young, regain youth: Pylius iuvenescere posset, O.

iuvenilis.definition: iuvenīlis e, adj. with comp. iuvenis, of youth, youthful, juvenile: dicendi impunitas: membra, Iu.: suis semper iuvenilior annis, O.: sidus iuvenile nepotes, a youthful constellation, O. —Plur n. as subst: iuvenilia l…

iuveniliter.definition: iuvenīliter adv. iuvenilis, after the manner of youth: exsultare.

iuvenis.definition: iuvenis is, adj. with comp. iūnior (once iuvenior, Ta.) DIV-, young, youthful: filius, Ta.: iuvenes anni, O.: iuvenes premere Medos, Iu.: toto iunior anno, H.: dis iunioribus permisit ut, etc.: quamvis iuvenior, adlig…

iuvenor.definition: iuvenor —, —, ārī, dep. iuvenis, to act with youthful indiscretion, wanton: teneris versibus, H.

iuventa.definition: iuventa ae, f iuvenis, the age of youth, youth: membra decora iuventā , V.: primā a parte iuventae: ita se a iuventā gessisse, L.: citra iuventam, in boyhood, O.—Youth, young folk: docilis, H.—Person., the goddess of …

iuventas.definition: iuventās ātis, f iuvenis, the age of youth, youth, V.; of the eagle, youthful vigor, H.—Person., youth, the goddess of youth, C.: comis, H.

iuventus.definition: iuventūs ūtis, f iuvenis, the age of youth, youth (from twenty to forty): quae iuventute geruntur et viribus: iuventutem suam exercuit, S. — Young persons, youth: pleraque, S.: omnis: Troiana, V.: Alcinoi, i. e. Phaea…
